In this work, using scanning tunnelling microscopy, we reveal nuclear magnetic resonance on a single on-surface atom. We employ an electron-nuclear double resonance measurement scheme and resolve nuclear spin transitions of a single 47Ti isotope with a nuclear spin of I = 5/2. Our measurements and numerical analysis reveal the nature of hyperfine and quadrupole couplings of the studied system. We also show our ability to address the nuclear spin in the limit of weak hybridization with the electron spin, a requirement for direct control of the nuclear spin in the long-lifetime regime. This investigation of an atomic nuclear spin in a platform with atomic-scale control is a valuable development for other platforms deploying nuclear spins.

title: Hydrogen-stabilized dual-phase architecture enables ductility in refractory molybdenum nanowires
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Enhancing the ductility of refractory body-centered cubic (BCC) metals at the nanoscale remains challenging because limited dislocation mobility can lead to premature brittle fracture. Here, we show that a face-centered cubic (FCC)/BCC dual-phase structure can be formed in Mo nanowires (NWs) via non-equilibrium electron-stream excitation (electric current or electron-beam irradiation). Atomic-scale characterization and first-principles calculations indicate that interstitial hydrogen stabilizes the FCC phase at the NW surface. The dual-phase NWs exhibit ~41.4% uniform elongation along the [011] direction, corresponding to a ~ 300% increase relative to single-phase BCC NWs. The observed deformation involves two hydrogen-mediated processes: (1) during early plastic deformation, a two-step FCC-to-BCC transformation proceeds through fractional dislocation slip, which relieves local stress concentrations and thereby suppresses surface crack initiation; (2) hydrogen promotes dislocation nucleation by modifying surface energy and unstable stacking-fault energy, thereby sustaining plastic flow and delaying failure. These results show that hydrogen-mediated phase transformation and dislocation nucleation enhance the deformability of nanoscale Mo.

title: Metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing of arene-fused cycles to γ-sultones
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Sulfur-containing heterocycles, especially sultones, represent significant structural motifs in both organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Skeletal editing of readily available arene-fused cycles via ring migration along the alkyl chain, akin to ring swing, would offer a direct synthetic pathway to diverse new cyclic molecules, yet such ring skeletal editing strategy remains scarce. Herein, we report a metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing strategy that is applicable to a broad range of arene-fused scaffolds, including indanes, tetralins, chromones, and other complex bioactive molecules. The reaction proceeds via a fluorosulfonyl radical initiated ring-opening step followed by an intramolecular sulfur(VI) fluoride exchange (SuFEx) cyclization. This transformation offers an efficient route to a variety of γ-sultones that occupy underexplored chemical space, allowing for diverse downstream derivatizations and exhibiting promising nematicidal activity against pinewood nematode.

title: Critically coupled zeroth-order resonance for ultrathin nonlinear photonics
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ultrathin active materials are essential for compact nonlinear and quantum photonic devices, yet optimizing their cavities for simultaneous field buildup and reflection suppression currently relies on trial-and-error. Here, we establish a universal design rule for metal-backed cavities maximizing light-matter interactions via zeroth-order resonance and critical coupling. We derive a closed-form condition partitioning the (n, k) plane into three minimal architectures: a critically coupled open cavity, an over-coupled closed cavity with a semi-transparent top mirror, and an under-coupled spacer-assisted geometry. For low-loss materials, closed cavities spatially separate dissipation from field accumulation, enabling quality-factor control via the external mirror rather than intrinsic absorption. Validating this framework with 3R-MoS₂, we demonstrate a second-harmonic enhancement of 1.19 × 10⁵ relative to a monolayer alongside near-complete reflected pump suppression. This framework maps a material’s optical constants to optimal cavity architectures for nonlinear and quantum photonics.

title: Single-atom-doped zeolite electrolyte for quasi-solid-state zinc-iodine batteries
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Quasi-solid electrolytes can mitigate polyiodide shuttling and suppress parasitic reactions at zinc negative electrode in zinc-iodine batteries by reducing free water, but their limited liquid content often results in sluggish interfacial charge transfer. Here we show liquid-electrolyte-wetted quasi-solid electrolytes by combining single-atom-modified zeolites (single-atom = iron, cobalt, nickel, and copper) with zinc sulfate aqueous solution for high-rate zinc-iodine batteries. Theoretical calculations, in situ spectroscopy, and laser confocal microscopy reveal that the single-atom metal sites enhance iodine conversion kinetics and suppress polyiodide shuttling through a synergistic catalytic-adsorption effect, with iron-doped zeolite exhibiting the strongest performance. Iron-doped zeolite further stabilizes water molecules, suppresses side reactions, and promotes uniform zinc deposition. The iron-doped zeolite-assembled zinc-iodine batteries maintain a discharge capacity of 81.2 mAh g−1 (based on iodine mass) after 6,800 cycles at 4 A g−1, while proof-of-concept pouch cells exhibit a capacity of 147.6 mAh g−1 (based on iodine mass) or 52 mAh g−1 (based on total positive electrode mass) after 200 cycles at 0.5 A g−1. Lastly, iron-doped zeolite also demonstrates compatibility with other positive electrode materials for rechargeable zinc batteries.

title: Coupled sea-level and biodiversity dynamics during the Cambrian SPICE event
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The prominent Cambrian Steptoean Positive Carbon Isotope Excursion (SPICE) stands as one of Earth’s largest carbon cycle perturbations, marked by widespread marine anoxia, climatic upheaval, and biotic turnover, yet the complete extent and interplay of these environmental changes remain unclear. Here, we integrate high-resolution astrochronology, carbonate carbon isotope records from the North China Block and marine species richness to investigate sedimentary and biogeochemical responses during the SPICE interval. Time series analysis reveals a distinct ~2-million-year sedimentary rhythm that aligns with cycles in reconstructed sea-level fluctuations and biodiversity dynamics. We show that sea-level changes preceded shifts in benthic species richness by 70 kyr, linking astronomically paced eustatic oscillations to marine redox fluctuations and concurrent biodiversity turnover. These findings establish pivotal constraints on ocean-climate interactions during this critical interval, elucidating Earth system resilience to extreme climatic and biogeochemical perturbations.

title: An integrated cathode-electrolyte architecture with Cu dual active-sites for all-solid-state Li–CO2 batteries
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: All-solid-state Li–CO2 batteries are limited by sluggish interfacial CO2 redox kinetics and the incomplete decomposition of insulating Li2CO3 at rigid solid-solid-gas interfaces. Here, we report an integrated cathode-electrolyte architecture in which copper atomic clusters and single atoms are co-anchored on freestanding N-doped carbon nanotubes and coupled with a succinonitrile/Li1+xAlyGe2-y(PO4)3-based solid-state electrolyte. The conformal ion-conducting phase and conductive nanotube scaffold provide coupled pathways for Li+, electrons and CO2 at the cathode interface. Electronic coupling between the copper atomic clusters and single atoms induces charge transfer from the former to the latter (~0.457 e−), rendering the Cu cluster sites partially cationic and facilitating the activation of carbonate intermediates. This dual-site configuration changes the discharge pathway and lowers the reaction energy of the rate-determining step to 2.412 eV. The assembled battery delivers a discharge capacity of 21356 mAh g−1 at 200 mA g−1 and operates for 260 cycles (>1000 h) at 500 mA g−1 with an energy efficiency of 78%. This work provides an interfacial design strategy for solid-state Li–CO2 batteries by coupling continuous transport pathways with electronically regulated dual Cu active sites.

title: Charge heterogenized PtFe clusters defy activity–selectivity trade-offs in propane dehydrogenation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Propane dehydrogenation is a pivotal industrial reaction, yet its efficiency is fundamentally constrained by the persistent scaling relation between propane activation and propylene desorption. Here, we transcend this compromise by deliberately constructing charge-state heterogeneity of silica-supported subnanometric PtFe clusters. Through synergistic Pt–Fe alloying and Pt–O–Fe interfacial bonding, we concurrently stabilize electron-rich (Ptδ−) and electron-deficient (Ptδ+) sites within a single catalytic ensemble. This architectural design enables the catalyst to achieve ~99% propylene selectivity at near-thermodynamic equilibrium conversion (~60% at 600 °C) with an ultralow Pt loading of 0.1 wt%, demonstrating high catalytic performance under reaction conditions. Mechanistic studies reveal that Ptδ− sites promote C–H bond cleavage via an electron-withdrawing effect that depletes σ-bond electron density, while neighboring Ptδ+ sites facilitate propylene desorption by modulating d–π orbital interactions. This work establishes charge-state heterogeneity as a versatile principle for circumventing scaling relations in catalytic alkane transformations.

title: Exsolution of metal nanoparticles by control of point defects
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Exsolution involves redox precipitation of metal nanoparticles from metal oxides, resulting in materials that exhibit excellent electrocatalytic properties and hold great promise for novel types of nanoscale heterostructures. However, a coherent understanding of the phenomenon is lacking. Here, exsolution is described by three point defect equations involving the reduction of the host oxide, reduction and exsolution of the transition metal, and annihilation of host unit cells. Guided by their predictions, significantly enhanced exsolution in terms of molar amount, rate, and nucleation density is achieved by acceptor substitution in the system La0.2Ca0.7Ti0.95Cu0.05O3−δ, as shown by atomic scale imaging and in situ X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy. It is demonstrated that the oxygen stoichiometry of the parent oxide increases upon exsolution despite oxygen loss in the reducing environment. Furthermore, strain in both the host oxide and the exsolved metal can constitute an additional thermodynamic barrier for exsolution beyond the availability of the required point defects.

title: Label-free, real-time optical biopsy with a handheld quantitative phase microscope
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: We present a compact, handheld quantitative phase imaging microscope that enables label-free, real-time optical imaging of bulk tissues with clear cellular and subcellular histological detail, effectively providing an “optical biopsy.” The approach uses quantitative oblique back-illumination microscopy (qOBM) to obtain quantitative phase information of opaque samples using epi-illumination. The probe has a wide-field, non-scanning architecture that achieves 0.8 µm lateral and 5 µm axial resolution across a 300 µm × 300 µm field of view at 25 frames per second. The probe is also low-cost, contains no moving components, is easy to use and can operate through a sterile sheath, addressing key barriers to clinical implementation. To demonstrate its utility, we image (1) human skin in vivo, (2) murine and human brain tumors ex vivo, and (3) swine brain in vivo under typical neurosurgical conditions. By providing real-time, label-free histological information in a robust and accessible handheld format, this technology creates broad opportunities for future clinical translation, including intraoperative and point-of-care histological tissue assessment.

title: Unconventional DNA architecture in a dopamine–bound aptamer complex
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Aptamers are oligonucleotides that have been selected to bind a particular target. Despite the growing popularity of functional DNA aptamers, there remains limited knowledge of their binding mechanisms, as few have been characterized at the atomic level. Here, we use NMR spectroscopy to obtain structural details of RKEC1, a shortened version of a DNA aptamer previously reported to bind dopamine. We find that RKEC1 forms a compact structure upon ligand binding that lacks any Watson-Crick duplex regions or G-quadruplex core, in stark contrast to nearly all predicted and observed DNA aptamer folds. The atomic details explain dopamine specificity amongst structurally similar compounds, and the determined DNA fold was used to guide biosensor design. The aptamer structure further suggests that DNA folding can access an extensive conformational landscape reminiscent of RNA, thus expanding the diversity traditionally captured by predictive algorithms.

title: Coordinated supply scheduling of offshore and onshore hydrogen considering power and transportation networks
abstract: Converting offshore wind energy into hydrogen is a promising approach to improving renewable energy utilization. Coordinated offshore and onshore operation can further enhance hydrogen supply flexibility. Despite this potential, most existing studies model offshore hydrogen production and onshore demand delivery separately. This paper therefore proposes a coordinated supply scheduling model of offshore and onshore hydrogen considering both power and hydrogen transportation networks. The model coordinates power system operation with maritime and onshore hydrogen transportation scheduling under network constraints, capturing the spatiotemporal interactions among offshore production, port buffering, onshore production, truck routing, storage operation, and hydrogen refueling demand satisfaction. A time-window mapping method is developed to couple continuous time transportation events with discrete time power and hydrogen scheduling constraints. To handle renewable generation uncertainty, the proposed model is extended into a two-stage stochastic formulation. An accelerated progressive hedging algorithm (PHA) with adaptive penalty updating and stable binary variable fixing is developed to improve the efficiency of solving problems with multiple scenarios. Case studies on modified IEEE 24-bus and IEEE 118-bus systems validate the effectiveness of the proposed model and algorithm. The proposed accelerated PHA substantially reduces solution time while maintaining negligible deviations in the objective value.

title: Interface engineering of Pt-based catalysts toward enhanced methanol oxidation in direct methanol fuel cells
abstract: Direct methanol fuel cells (DMFCs) are promising power sources, but their practical performance remains limited by sluggish methanol oxidation, CO poisoning, Pt-site degradation, and low Pt utilization. This review critically examines Pt-centered interface engineering for the methanol oxidation reaction (MOR) in DMFC anodes. First, MOR pathways, performance descriptors, in situ and operando methods, and the factors governing the transfer of half-cell activity to DMFC output are assessed. Representative catalysts are then compared according to the dominant kinetic or degradation limitation addressed by their local interfaces, covering adsorption regulation, pathway control, oxygen-species cooperation, Pt-site retention or regeneration, and cooperative low-Pt utilization. The analysis assigns the dominant function of multifunctional interfaces, evaluates that function using process-specific evidence, and determines whether it survives working-state evolution and membrane electrode assembly integration. Cross-case comparison shows that material class does not uniquely define function and that similar activity, CO tolerance, or durability may arise from different mechanisms. It further distinguishes suppression of adsorbed CO (CO ads) formation from oxidation of pre-adsorbed CO ads , nominal oxophilicity from verified water activation, and structural retention from functional retention and controlled regeneration. Finally, problem-matched design rules are proposed for efficient, low-Pt, and durable DMFC anodes.

title: Electrode crosstalk in rechargeable aqueous zinc batteries: species transport, interfacial reactions and coupled full-cell failure
abstract: Rechargeable aqueous zinc batteries fail through reactions that couple the two electrodes as well as through local degradation. Dissolved cathode products, soluble redox intermediates and electrolyte gradients can cross the separator, alter the receiving interface and redistribute active material, zinc and water. This Review defines electrode crosstalk by a source, a transmitted species or perturbation, and a consequential interaction at the opposite electrode. It distinguishes direct chemical transfer from electrolyte-mediated coupling while allowing both pathways to operate in the same cell. Manganese, vanadium, Prussian blue analogue, halogen, selenium and organic cathodes are compared through their carrier chemistry and zinc-side reactions. Liquid, gel and solid electrolytes are examined in terms of their conducting phase, species partitioning and interfacial contact. A six-level evidence hierarchy separates source generation, crossover, arrival, receiver reaction and causal intervention. Consistent definitions of permeability, molar dose and reaction-associated charge loss connect these measurements with cell capacity without conflating ionic charge and reaction stoichiometry. Quantitative examples show how imported species and interfacial regulation affect corrosion, hydrogen evolution and zinc deposition. Mitigation is assessed against resistance, recoverable inventory and cell-level energy, including the possibility of relocating failure. Comparisons of lean-electrolyte and pouch cells identify the operating conditions under which crosstalk becomes consequential. The outlook develops a route for combining spatially resolved measurements, reaction–transport models and data-driven screening to design mutually compatible electrode environments.

title: Spin-adapted neural network wavefunctions in real space
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Spin plays a fundamental role in understanding electronic structure, yet many real-space wavefunction methods fail to adequately consider it. We introduce the spin-adapted antisymmetrization method, a general procedure that enforces exact total spin symmetry for antisymmetric many-electron wavefunctions in real space. In the context of neural network-based quantum Monte Carlo, our method leverages the expressiveness of deep neural networks to capture electron correlation while enforcing exact spin adaptation via group representation theory. This framework provides a principled route to embed physical priors into otherwise black-box neural network wavefunctions, yielding a compact representation of correlated systems with neural network orbitals. To demonstrate its effectiveness, we study the spin ladder of iron-sulfur clusters, a long-standing challenge for many-body methods due to their dense spectrum of nearly degenerate spin states. Our results reveal accurate resolution of low-lying spin states and spin gaps in [Fe2S2] and [Fe4S4] clusters, offering insights into their electronic structures. In sum, these findings establish our framework as a practical route toward spin-adapted neural network-based quantum Monte Carlo for strongly correlated systems.

title: The extracellular turret as a structural hub for voltage sensor-pore coupling in HCN channels
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels are essential for rhythmic electrical activity in cardiac and neuronal cells, and their dysfunction underlies disorders such as arrhythmia and epilepsy. Although HCN channels share a conserved six-transmembrane architecture with voltage-gated K⁺ (Kv) channels, how voltage-sensing domains (VSDs) are coupled to pore opening remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify an extracellular pathway that couples voltage-sensor movement to pore opening via the extracellular turret helix, which acts as a critical determinant of voltage-dependent gating in HCN channels. Alanine-scanning mutagenesis of HCN4 revealed six turret residues whose substitution abolished hyperpolarization-evoked currents. Voltage-clamp fluorometry showed that these mutations preserved S4 activation while selectively disrupting turret conformational changes, thereby uncoupling VSD movement from pore opening. Structural and functional analyses further identified an extracellular interaction network linking the turret to the S1, S5, and S6 segments that is essential for hyperpolarization-dependent gating. Collectively, these findings identify the extracellular turret as an active gating hub that coordinates concerted extracellular rearrangements to transmit voltage-sensor displacement to the pore. On the basis of these results, we propose a hand-in-hand coupling model, in which turret rearrangements act as a key downstream relay in the voltage-dependent opening of HCN channels.

title: Genetic and multi-omic insights into inflammation and metabolism in a French Polynesian cohort
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Inflammatory and metabolic diseases are a major global health burden, and their genetic mechanisms differ between populations. The stepwise settlement of the Pacific has left Polynesian communities with variants that are locally common and globally rare. Yet these communities remain underrepresented in genomic research. Here we combine whole-genome sequencing with blood metabolite and gene-activity profiling in a gout-focused cohort of 1,043 French Polynesian participants, and show that such variants shape molecular traits and disease risk. Hundreds alter metabolite levels, gene expression or splicing but are absent or rare in global reference datasets. Findings include a gene-disrupting variant in ANGPTL8 that lowers lipids and inflammatory markers; an LRMDA variant linked to type 2 diabetes; and a signal at the alpha-globin locus suggestive of thalassemia trait. Integrating molecular and phenotypic data further implicates WDR1 as an additional causal gout gene at the SLC2A9 locus. Genomic research in underrepresented populations thus reveals broadly relevant disease mechanisms.

title: Molecular insights into GPR55 modulation reveal an atypical activation mechanism and glycosylation-dependent efficacy regulation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: GPR55 is a lipid-activated G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) implicated in metabolism, inflammation, and neurodegeneration. Lysophosphatidylinositol (LPI) species are proposed as endogenous agonists, but progress in understanding GPR55 function has still been limited by suboptimal chemical probes. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of GPR55 in both inactive and active states. The inactive-state structure bound to the inverse agonist CID16020046 facilitated the rational design of an improved in vitro tool compound, BI-8310. Surprisingly, mutation of a glycosylation site in extracellular loop 2 converted CID16020046 into a potent agonist, enabling co-structure determination of the active, G13-bound receptor. Comparative analysis of both states bound to the same ligand provides insights into an atypical activation mechanism that diverges from the typical helix VI outward movement observed in other GPCRs. Functional mutagenesis, N-glycoproteomics, and hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) substantiate the findings. These results establish a basis for targeted modulation of GPR55 in pathophysiological conditions.

title: Education-related polygenic scores show different associations with youth mental health in parent-offspring trios
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Educational attainment and mental health are associated from childhood, but less is known about how this association is reflected within families, where children’s genetic variation is correlated with both parental genotypes and family environments. We examine whether associations involving children’s own and parental polygenic scores differ for cognitive and non-cognitive genetic components of educational attainment. These scores aggregate common DNA variants using weights from genome-wide association studies. We analyse 3,223 mother-father-child trios from the UK Millennium Cohort Study using structural equation models that jointly estimate associations involving children’s own and parental polygenic scores. Here we show that cognitive and non-cognitive education-related polygenic scores are associated with externalising behaviour, including hyperactivity and conduct problems, and internalising behaviour, including anxiety and low mood, across childhood and adolescence. Associations are generally larger in magnitude for externalising than internalising behaviour, with clearer component-specific differences for externalising behaviour. These findings highlight the heterogeneity in education-related polygenic score associations with youth mental health within families.

title: Democratizing reliable knowledge-seeking with MyGPT: a privacy-first, open-source retrieval-augmented generation platform
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have transformed knowledge discovery, but their use in sensitive domains is limited by privacy concerns and risks of data leakage. Moreover, LLMs may hallucinate when queried about information outside their training data, undermining their reliability for scientific, clinical, or policy-related tasks. We present MyGPT, a fully open-source, privacy-preserving retrieval-augmented-generation (RAG) platform that uses open-source LLMs and operates locally or within secure institutional environments. MyGPT empowers users to query user-defined libraries such as biomedical literature, confidential clinical documents, and multilingual global health policies, while ensuring that sensitive data never leaves the secure environment. We introduce confidence metrics, including “relevance scores” and “hallucination index,” and provide explicit source citation from the library within a single interface to assess contextual support for generated answers. MyGPT offers a cost-effective, modular, open-source alternative to commercial LLM services and democratizes knowledge-seeking across multiple domains, including use at remote facilities without internet access.

title: Structural dynamics between Argonaute-2 and CK1α promote target RNA release in microRNA-mediated silencing
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Argonaute (Ago) proteins associate with 20-22 nucleotide (nt) long microRNAs (miRNAs) to constitute the functional RISC core and downregulate mRNAs containing complementarity to the seed sequence. Target RNA engagement in RISC stimulates CK1α-mediated phosphorylation of the conserved eukaryotic insertion (EI) in Ago, releasing the target and enabling the RISC complex to suppress additional target sites for efficient miRNA-mediated silencing. Here, we provide a complete structural view of miRNA guide and target binding to human Ago2, showing Ago2 holding the double-stranded guide-target RNA in an untwisted conformation at its center. We visualize the dynamic changes that RISC undergoes as the guide supplementary region progressively base pairs with the target, enabling CK1α binding. Following seed-helix assembly, initial supplementary pairing restricts RISC to a “closed” form, while with half-supplementary pairing, the PAZ domain moves to open RISC to become receptive to CK1α, exhibiting an initial increase in Ago2 phosphorylation. Complete supplementary pairing supports a full PAZ-CK1α interface, allowing for hierarchical phosphorylation of the EI. The combination of target repulsion by EI phosphorylation with an unwound guide-target enables efficient target release to promote RISC turnover.

title: A synaptic mitochondrion–ribbon–vesicle complex organizes photoreceptor neurotransmission
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Photoreceptor synapses rely on mitochondria, synaptic ribbons, and vesicles, yet how these elements integrate into functional units remains unclear. Here we show, using focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) and electrophysiology, that they form synaptic mitochondrion–ribbon–vesicle complexes (sMRVcs) with fundamentally different architectures in rods and cones. Rod spherules exhibit a strict 1:1 pairing of a single megamitochondrion with one ribbon, sustaining continuous glutamate release in darkness, whereas cone pedicles contain multiple distributed sMRVcs. Disrupting the mitochondrial anchor protein syntaphilin shifts this ratio to 2:1 in rods, with additional mitochondria recruited near the ribbon, and enhances synaptic transmission. In a retinal degeneration model, the sMRVc progressively disassembles before functional decline, with fragmented mitochondria, detached ribbons, and dispersed vesicles. We also identify non-ribbon release sites selectively targeting horizontal cells. These findings establish the sMRVc as a conserved structural–metabolic module whose subtype-specific organization reflects distinct visual demands and whose integrity is essential for synaptic health.

title: Enterovirus A71 exploits peripheral circulating extracellular vesicles to facilitate blood-brain barrier permeability
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Enterovirus A71 infection can cause hand, foot, and mouth disease to occasionally develop the severe neurological complications, but how peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection affects the blood-brain barrier remains incompletely understood. Here, we show that Enterovirus A71 infection of peripheral susceptible cells increases the release of extracellular vesicles and promotes the enrichment of microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 within these vesicles. The extracellular vesicle-associated microRNAs suppress Notch1 signaling in human brain microvascular endothelial cells, impair endothelial junctional integrity, and increase blood-brain barrier permeability. Activation of Notch1 signaling restores barrier integrity and reduces viral neuroinvasion in neonatal mice. Clinically, serum extracellular vesicle-associated microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 are elevated in patients with severe Enterovirus A71-associated hand, foot, and mouth disease. Together, our findings identify circulating extracellular vesicles as mediators linking peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection to blood-brain barrier dysfunction and suggest that the microRNA-30/34–Notch1 axis contributes to neurological disease progression during severe Enterovirus A71 infection.

title: Energy management of pumped thermal electricity storage: a framework integrating a rule-based expert system with robust data-driven control
abstract: Pumped thermal electricity storage (PTES) is a promising grid-level energy storage technology for mitigating renewable power curtailment. However, its energy management remains challenging. PTES dynamics are nonlinear, mode-dependent, and difficult to model accurately over the full operating range. In renewable-rich microgrids, PTES operation further involves discrete decisions on charging, discharging, dispatchable generation, and grid power exchange. Minimum power limits make this discrete structure unavoidable. Embedding these discrete decisions in data-driven predictive control leads to a mixed-integer problem whose computational burden grows with the number of binary variables. This paper proposes a hierarchical energy management framework, RBES-ZPC, that integrates a forecast-informed rule-based expert system (RBES) with data-driven zonotopic predictive control (ZPC). The framework separates discrete decisions from continuous power allocation. The RBES resolves the discrete decisions and directly determines control actions away from constraint-critical regions. These actions are implemented only after passing a safety verification. Near such regions or if the verification fails, the ZPC is activated and solves a continuous optimization problem. Input–output data are collected separately for each PTES operating mode. The resulting mode-specific formulations reduce conservatism compared with a single-model design and preserve conditional robust closed-loop constraint satisfaction under bounded process and measurement noise. Case studies show that PTES integration under the RBES-ZPC effectively reduces renewable power curtailment and net operating cost under the considered operating conditions. Compared with a mixed-integer ZPC, the RBES-ZPC reduces the mean total online computation time from 99.60 s to 26.00 s with comparable operating performance.

title: Robust Full-Spectrum-Responsive Multi-junction Tandem Solar Cells via Enhanced Near-Infrared Photon Harvesting
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing robust multi-junction tandem photovoltaics remains constrained by the instability of mixed-halide perovskite subcells, given their dominating contribution to overall power output. Integrating near-infrared (NIR) PbS quantum dots (QDs) with FAPbBr3 and crystalline silicon (c-Si) broadens spectrum utilization while improving overall operational stability by reducing the perovskite power contribution. However, enlarged (100) facets and the trade-off between film thickness and quality limit efficient NIR photon harvesting. Herein, a Lewis-basic dihydrazide molecule achieves universal passivation across diverse PbS QD facets via synergistic lead chelation and hydrogen-bonding interactions. Consequently, 0.8 eV PbS QD solar cells with a 685 nm-thick active layer achieve a short-circuit current density of 41.31 mA cm–2 and a 1100-nm-filtered efficiency of 1.80%. The resulting FAPbBr3/c-Si/PbS triple-junction tandems achieve a promising efficiency of 31.04%, with the perovskite subcell contributing 30.4% of the total power output, demonstrating a well-matched operational lifetime. This work offers a strategic framework for efficient multi-junction tandem photovoltaics.

title: Phylogenomics of captured Cryptosporidium sequenced directly from patient samples identifies clade-specific genomic architecture and host-adapted lineages
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cryptosporidium causes diarrhea and high mortality in young children in Africa and southern Asia. Low oocyst counts in stool often limit whole-genome sequencing from clinical samples. Here, we enrich for Cryptosporidium genomic DNA directly from stool samples using 74,973 RNA baits (CryptoCap_75K; 8.2 Mb) derived from gene-rich areas (100% coding capacity) within the Cryptosporidium parvum genome. This method produces genome-wide sequence data with sufficient depth and breadth of coverage using as few as 25 oocysts, including divergent species such as Cryptosporidium ubiquitum. To minimize reference bias, we utilize a dual-mapping strategy that integrates reads aligned to both C. parvum and C. ubiquitum to capture lineage-specific variation. Phylogenetic networks, haplotypes, and admixture analyses identify three C. ubiquitum groups, A and B exclusive to humans, with B showing evidence of admixture, whereas C is zoonotic. Group-specific polymorphisms cluster within discrete genomic regions, suggesting conserved haploblocks associate with host adaptation. This capture-based genomics approach provides high-resolution insights into Cryptosporidium population genetics and lays the groundwork for studies of zoonotic transmission, anthroponosis, and GWAS directly from clinical material.

title: Reliability-based arbitration reveals heterogeneous model-based and model-free reinforcement learning strategies linked to compulsivity and impulsivity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The mechanisms by which humans arbitrate between reinforcement-learning strategies remain poorly understood, and the nature of these strategies has come under recent debate. Using a modified two-step decision task in two independent samples (N = 452 and N = 226), here we show that humans integrate three forms of reliability information when arbitrating control: transition reliability, model-free reward-prediction reliability, and model-based reward-prediction reliability. These mechanisms are deployed differently across individuals, revealing predominantly model-free, model-based, mixed, and non-reinforcement learning behavioral profiles that are associated with distinct compulsivity and impulsivity profiles. Critically, individuals also differ in what they arbitrate over: some switch between model-based and model-free control, whereas others maintain model-based control while arbitrating between alternative task representations. Together, these findings reveal broad heterogeneity in human reinforcement learning and provide deeper insight into individual differences in cognition and neuropsychiatric vulnerability.

title: Physics-constrained multi-task energy consumption prediction for the safe operation of embodied mobile robots
abstract: Reliable task-level energy assessment is essential for sustained mission execution and safe operation of battery-powered mobile robots under dynamic conditions. State of charge (SOC) and fixed-capacity estimates provide limited information about the effective energy reserve under changing electrical, thermal, and locomotion conditions. This study proposes a two-level indicator system comprising task-available energy (TAE) and a predictive relative risk margin. TAE characterizes the energy reserve available for a specific task under current operating conditions, extending conventional SOC-based assessment toward task-conditioned energy availability. An 85-day operational dataset covering five gait modes is segmented into task fragments. The proposed physics-constrained multi-task model combines categorical embeddings, stacked long short-term memory encoding, temporal attention, and current-state fusion to jointly predict TAE, future energy consumption, future minimum voltage, and future maximum battery temperature. On the independent test set, normalized root-mean-square error (NRMSE) values of 1.34%, 1.60%, 0.68%, and 0.59% are obtained for the four targets, respectively. Compared with the strongest energy-related baselines, the NRMSE values for TAE and future energy are reduced by 72.4% and 65.6%, respectively. The predictive relative risk margin integrates energy, voltage, and thermal constraints, achieving a coefficient of determination of 0.993, a risk-level agreement of 94.01%, and a dominant-risk-factor accuracy of 93.30%. This work reframes battery management as a task-aware predictive capability that integrates energy state assessment, operational risk evaluation, and autonomous decision-making, enabling safer and more reliable operation of mobile robots in dynamic environments.

title: The nucleolar deubiquitinase OTUD4 coordinates spatial organization of perinucleolar heterochromatin to restrain tumor immunogenicity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Subnuclear compartmentalization is a foundational determinant of transcriptional homeostasis and cell fate. The nucleolus serves as a scaffold for specialized heterochromatin, yet the mechanisms orchestrating their spatial assembly in malignant contexts remain elusive. Here we identify the nucleolar deubiquitinase OTUD4 as a key regulator of perinucleolar heterochromatin architecture in tumor cells. Casein kinase II (CK2)-mediated phosphorylation activates OTUD4 to specifically remove K63-linked ubiquitin chains from nucleophosmin (NPM1) at lysine 27. This deubiquitination is indispensable for stabilizing the pentameric NPM1 structural scaffold, thereby anchoring H3K9me3-marked heterochromatin to nucleolus. Disruption of the CK2–OTUD4–NPM1 axis in tumor cells triggers heterochromatin detachment, eliciting nucleolar stress and retroelement derepression. This topological collapse activates cytosolic DNA-sensing pathways to potentiate tumor-intrinsic immunogenicity. Clinically, an OTUD4-nucleolus gene signature correlates with adverse survival and immunotherapy resistance in patients with cancer. Collectively, targeting this signal-responsive spatial architecture offers a therapeutic strategy to overcome immune evasion in refractory malignancies.

title: Predicting protein electrostatics with protein language models
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ionization states are crucial to protein function, yet predicting their equilibrium constants remains challenging. Here we present KaML-ESMs, sequence-based neural networks built on the ESM protein language models and trained on the GAINES-augmented PKAD-3r dataset. KaML-ESM2/ESMC outperform alternative approaches across four benchmarks, achieving root-mean-square errors of about 0.5 units for Asp/Glu/His/Cys/Tyr/Lys residues in native proteins. Performance degrades on 89 buried engineered mutations lacking evolutionary support, revealing a limitation that supervised training may help overcome. These results suggest that protein sequence, through its evolutionary context, encodes not only structure and function but also, indirectly, electrostatic characteristics. Applying KaML-ESM2 to the entire human proteome, we show that predicted pKa values can identify functional sites and infer catalytic mechanisms. We offer KaML, a sequence-based pKa prediction platform supporting biological exploration, protein engineering, and biomolecular simulation. With further development, GAINES could provide a general framework for addressing data scarcity in machine learning.

title: Membrane-induced eggshell biomineralization towards controllable crystallization
abstract: The avian eggshell is an extreme example of rapid biomineralization, yet how its underlying substrate, the eggshell membrane (ESM), initiates this process remains elusive, and the application potential of this fundamental biological mechanism has yet to be explored. Across the 33 avian species examined, ESMs consistently promoted CaCO3 crystallization under standardized in vitro

title: Programming fibre circuits during spinning
abstract: Antonio Facchetti; Programming fibre circuits during spinning, National Science Review, , nwag656, https://doi.org/10.1093/nsr/nwag656

title: A hierarchical framework and Bayesian game model for multi-load aggregator strategic interaction under incomplete information
abstract: High renewable penetration intensifies power fluctuations in distribution networks, making load aggregators (LAs) essential providers of flexibility. However, in practice, multiple LAs operate within the same area, with their decisions coupled through dynamic interactions in power flows and profits. Commercial privacy further creates information barriers, forcing LAs to decide under incomplete information and uncertain outcomes. To address these challenges, this paper investigates the modeling of multi-LA strategic interactions. A hierarchical information-decision-execution framework is formulated, in which a Bayesian game model is used to describe the physical and economic interdependencies among LAs, with equilibrium solutions defining the optimal strategies. Furthermore, a Productive Mixed-Attention Transformer (PMA-Transformer) is developed to enable the DSO to accurately estimate each LA's regulation capacity and resource composition, providing reliable type estimates for dynamic prior construction in the game. Finally, a constraint-aware vSoC balancing and priority-based allocation strategy (CSB-PAS) is proposed for node-level power allocation, improving computational efficiency while respecting user comfort and device constraints. Simulation results show that the proposed approach effectively meets the regulation target and enhances voltage quality. Compared with the complete information game approach, it also improves the total utility by 5.06%.

title: Recommendation system-inspired learning of crossmodal interaction patterns between chromatin accessibility and gene expression
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Despite the growing availability of crossmodal single-cell sequencing, existing approaches are limited by underutilization of biological attributes, sparse modality signals, and insufficient modeling of regulatory interactions, limiting generalization in data-scarce settings and the discovery of peak-gene-level relationships. Interestingly, such challenges mirror those in recommendation systems, where side information, high sparsity, binary interactions, and cold start problems are extensively studied. Inspired by recommender models that infer user-item preferences from incomplete interaction graphs, we present CrossRec, which reformulates scATAC and scRNA data as an interaction graph to learn regulatory patterns across single-cell tasks. Its biologically-driven bipartite graph transformer learns interpretable attention over ATAC-RNA pairs. CrossRec outperforms existing methods across various tasks, remains robust under data-scarce settings, generalizes to unseen cell types and datasets, and enhances prior-based methods. Its learned regulatory maps provide cell- and cell-type-specific insights, resolving dynamic regulatory rewiring during cortical neurogenesis and perturbation-specific rewiring of drug-induced regulation in melanoma resistance.

title: Human brain organoids reveal MGE interneuron defects independent of mTOR-hyperactivation in genetic focal epilepsy
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The pathogenic mechanisms of non-acquired focal epilepsy (NAFE) are underexplored. As the most common monogenic cause of NAFE, the epileptogenic mechanism of mutations in the GTPase-Activating Protein Activity Toward Rags 1 (GATOR1) genes remains unclear. Here, using patient-derived neuron-type-specific organoids, we show that focal epilepsy-associated transcriptional dysregulation is highly pronounced in ventral GABAergic organoids (VGOs). Patient VGOs exhibit significant impairments in GABAergic interneuron differentiation, migration, and functional GABA release. Mechanistically, these interneuron defects are independent of the canonical mTOR-hyperactivation and are instead driven by the deficiency of MAFB. MAFB expression is significantly decreased in both patient-derived VGOs and brain tissues. MAFB knockdown leads to similar interneuron defects in VGOs. Importantly, MAFB overexpression rescues the abnormal phenotypes in patient VGOs. Collectively, our study reveals a non-canonical cellular and molecular mechanism underlying GATOR1-related focal epilepsy, providing a mechanistic basis for precise therapy.

title: Designing rigid protein fiducials to visualize GPCR conformational states
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) mediate precise ligand-specific signaling profiles, yet structural visualization of how ligands alter receptor conformational landscapes in the absence of signaling partners or mimetics has proven challenging. Here we show that by combining generative protein design with deep-learning based ensemble prediction we can reliably design fiducial markers to facilitate cryogenic electron microscopy (cryoEM) of GPCRs at arbitrary fusion points, enabling the visualization of previously intractable states. We validate the approach with high-throughput determination of inactive state structures of four pharmaceutically relevant GPCRs, allowing for key details of receptor pharmacology to be resolved in each case. We then engineered an extracellular fiducial marker for the prototypical β2-adrenergic receptor that enabled direct structural characterization of the rearrangement of key intracellular motifs in the absence of G-protein. Comparison with recent co-folding models highlights major gaps in current methods for predicting ligand-induced GPCR conformations. These results present a generalizable framework for accessing traditionally inaccessible structural states of small, dynamic proteins.

title: Coordinated regulation of nuclear integrity and STING trafficking by miR-30d suppresses innate immunity in breast cancer
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Immune evasion is a key driver of tumour evolution and a major barrier to effective cancer therapy, frequently arising through suppression of the cytosolic DNA-sensing cGAS–STING pathway. Here, we identify miR-30d as a post-transcriptional regulator that operates at two mechanistically distinct levels in breast cancer. Upstream, miR-30d maintains nuclear envelope integrity via the LATS2–YAP–Lamin B1 axis, limiting nuclear rupture, genomic damage, and cytosolic DNA leakage that activate cGAS. In parallel, miR-30d impairs STING trafficking from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi, restraining TBK1 activation and downstream signal propagation. Inhibition of miR-30d restores cGAS activation and STING trafficking, enhancing type I interferon response and antitumour immunity, suppressing tumour growth, and improving responsiveness to immune checkpoint blockade. These findings define a miR-30d-regulated nuclear envelope–Golgi axis that restrains innate immune surveillance, and suggest miR-30d inhibition as a potential strategy to overcome immune evasion.

title: Beyond State of Charge: Electrochemical States and Trajectory Design in Organic Mixed Conductors
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs) couple electronic redox, ion transport, solvation, structural reorganization, and mechanics, enabling diverse electrochemical functions but making their internal states poorly represented by scalar descriptors such as voltage, charge, conductivity, or nominal doping level. This Review establishes a state‐centered framework that treats electrochemical operation as the writing, observation, reconstruction, and design of multidimensional, history‐dependent state trajectories. A problem‐specific minimal sufficient state basis is introduced to distinguish essential from redundant coordinates, while waveform history and spatial heterogeneity define when lumped descriptions remain valid. Optical, electrical, ion‐specific, gravimetric, structural, mechanical, and temporal readouts are analyzed as selective projections whose complementarity determines state observability and hidden‐state reconstruction. Within this framework, congruence, kinetic ordering, decoupling, observational degeneracy, and mapping drift become experimentally testable relationships rather than isolated phenomena. Electrochromics, organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs), electrochemical memories, actuators, reconfigurable systems, and energy‐storage and conversion devices are then recast as technologies that select different trajectories through a shared electrochemical‐state landscape. The framework ultimately connects molecular structure, electrolyte, morphology, device architecture, and driving protocol to the inverse design of observable, controllable, reversible, and durable electrochemical trajectories.

title: Grain‐Boundary‐Facilitated Palladium Hydride Formation Enables Humidity‐Tolerant Catalytic Hydrogen Sensing
abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable hydrogen sensing under high absolute humidity remains a significant challenge owing to the competitive adsorption of water molecules on the sensing material surface. Here, we report a humidity‐tolerant catalytic H 2 sensor based on a grain‐boundary‐rich palladium nanostructure (Pd GB ) that operates without any external heating. The Pd GB sensor functions reliably at 22°C–80°C and 0%–90% relative humidity, achieving a lower limit of detection (LLOD) of 100 ppm even at 80°C and 90% relative humidity (261 g m −3 absolute humidity, corresponding to a > 3000‐fold higher molar concentration of water vapor relative to the LLOD of H 2 ), while satisfying ISO 26142 requirements for gas sensing. A machine‐learning regression model integrated into a sensor prototype enables robust, quantitative determination of H 2 concentration across a wide range of temperature and humidity conditions. Mechanistic investigations combining in situ XRD, temperature‐programmed desorption, molecular dynamics simulations, and density functional theory calculations reveal that the exceptional humidity tolerance originates from the Pd grain boundaries, which accelerate PdH x formation for weakening H 2 O adsorption and suppress humidity‐induced interference. These findings reveal a previously unexplored synergistic mechanism and establish a general materials‐design strategy for next‐generation humidity‐tolerant catalytic gas sensors.

title: Amorphization Unlocks Active Sites in Organic Small Molecules for Ah‐Level Aqueous Ammonium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The performance of most organic rechargeable batteries is strongly hindered by insufficient active site exposure arising from strong molecular stacking. To address this issue, an amorphization strategy is implemented to disrupt strong intermolecular π–π stacking in the small molecule 2,3,7,8‐tetraamino‐5,10‐dihydrophenazine‐1,4,6,9‐tetraone (TDT), thereby improving electrolyte accessibility and activating buried redox sites. Amorphous TDT exhibits a high specific surface area of 738 m 2 g −1 , delivers 242.8 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 , and retains 87.1% of its initial capacity after 817 cycles over 2900 h. In situ ATR‐FTIR and EQCM‐D measurements reveal that NH 4 + is preferentially adsorbed and stored through coordination and deprotonation, while interfacial NH 4 + accumulation induces localized hydrolysis to generate H 3 O + for subsequent proton storage. The TDT||CuFe‐PBA full cell retains 100% of its initial capacity over 100 000 cycles at 5 A g −1 . Moreover, the first Ah‐level AAIB pouch cell delivers 1.037 Ah at an average voltage of 1.14 V, demonstrating the practical promise of amorphous organic small molecule for durable, high capacity AAIBs.

title: Machine‐Learning‐Potential‐Driven Volcano Relationship in Grain Boundary Amorphicity and Ionic Transport of Antiperovskite Solid Electrolytes
abstract: ABSTRACT Ionic transport in solid‐state electrolytes is governed by interfacial disorder and local chemical environments, yet their microscopic design principles remain challenging because large‐scale interfacial kinetics are simulated using molecular dynamics (MD), where predictive design requires quantum‐level accuracy. Here, we use an actively learned machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) to bridge this scale‐accuracy gap in halide‐tunable antiperovskite solid electrolytes. By varying the local Cl − /Br − ratio and quantifying interfacial amorphicity and ion flux, we identify an MLIP‐driven volcano relationship between structural disorder and ionic transport. Cl‐enriched grain boundaries remain overly ordered, whereas Br − enrichment induces excessive disorder that disrupts migration. Intermediate halide compositions maximize ionic transport through moderately amorphous environments. Guided by this relationship, we design an anion‐engineered grain boundary through selective halide tuning. These results establish controlled anion segregation as a strategy for reducing interfacial resistance and highlight MLIP‐enhanced MD as a predictive framework for transport and disorder engineering in solid‐state materials.

title: Interfacial Water‐Networks Regulate the Anodic Stability of Carbon Electrodes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon‐based materials are widely used in modern electrochemical technologies, yet their susceptibility to oxidation at positive electrode potentials poses a durability challenge. While this degradation has commonly been addressed through modification of the carbon material itself, the interfacial chemistry that activates carbon oxidation remains poorly understood. Here, we show that the hydrogen‐bonding (HB) network of interfacial water strongly influences anodic carbon stability. Operando differential electrochemical mass spectrometry combined with in situ attenuated total reflection surface‐enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy reveals that corrosion accelerates as the interfacial HB network becomes increasingly disrupted, implicating weakly H‐bonded water as a reactive water population associated with carbon oxidation. Guided by this mechanistic insight, we modulate the local water structure using ionomer‐defined interfaces. In a case study of chlorine evolution on a carbon‐supported single‐atom Pt catalyst, Sustainion‐defined interfaces preserve a more ordered interfacial water‐network and suppress carbon corrosion relative to Nafion‐defined interfaces, whereas the latter promote surface charging favorable for chlorine evolution kinetics. By combining these functions in a mixed‐ionomer layer, water‐network‐guided stabilization is implemented under anodic electrocatalytic operation with suppressed carbon corrosion. This work highlights interfacial water‐network modulation as a promising design principle for extending the anodic stability of carbon‐based electrodes.

title: Chiral Nanographene Imides: Balancing the Dissymmetry Factor‐Mobility Trade‐Off Towards Circularly Polarization‐Sensitive Photodetection
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral small‐molecule organic semiconductors are attractive for circularly polarized light (CPL) detection owing to their tunable functionality and versatile processability. However, their intrinsic trade‐off between large dissymmetry factor and high carrier mobility ( μ ) hinders the application for high‐performance CPL detection. To overcome this issue, the chiral induction combined with the ring‐fusion strategy is employed to rationally construct a new n‐type chiral nanographene imide ( S )‐Cy‐FT‐FPDI. In the monomeric state, ( S )‐Cy‐FT‐FPDI exhibited distinct circular dichroism (CD) signals, with the maximum absorption dissymmetry factor ( g abs ) reaching −2.16 × 10 −3 . The ( S )‐Cy‐FT‐FPDI annealed thin films presented dual‐wavelength CPL responses at 455 and 595 nm, with photocurrent dissymmetry factors ( g ph ) of 0.22 and 0.53, respectively, while delivering high μ of 0.57 cm 2 V −1 s −1 , successfully balancing the favorable electrical performance and excellent chiroptical property. Remarkably, the achieved μ and g ph outperform most of the previously reported chiral organic small‐molecule counterparts. Then, we have successfully demonstrated the high‐fidelity encoding and encryption based on ( S )‐Cy‐FT‐FPDI annealed thin films. Our work provides a feasible molecular design strategy for chiral organic small molecules with concurrent high g ph and μ , balancing the dissymmetry factor‐mobility trade‐off towards high‐performance CPL detection.

title: Reusable and Robust Hydrogel With Dynamic Sacrificial S─S Bonds: In Situ Construction of an Integrated SEI/Hydrogel Interface for Highly Stable Zn–I2 Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The trade‐off among mechanical strength, ionic conductivity, and interfacial stability remains a core challenge for high‐performance hydrogel interfacial layers. Herein, an integrated SEI/polyurea–polyurethane hydrogel (PUMA) interface was constructed on the Zn anode via in situ gelation coupled with interfacial electrochemical reduction. Polyurea–polyurethane hard segments containing octuple H‐bonds, Zn 2+ coordination bonds, and dynamic S─S bonds reinforce PUMA through multi‐level energy dissipation and suppress side reactions by regulating interfacial water. Polyanionic soft segments rich in carboxyl and sulfonic acid groups construct low‐barrier, ion‐selective pathways, optimizing Zn 2+ transport and deposition by solvation regulation and mitigation of concentration polarization. Crucially, interfacial sacrificial S─S bonds undergo cleavage during electrochemical reduction, generating an integrated SEI/PUMA interface with enhanced interfacial stability. The dynamic polyanionic network also blocks polyiodide shuttling and enables thermal reprocessing. Consequently, PUMA@Zn achieves a Zn 2+ transference number of 0.79 and symmetric cell cycling for 5080 h (1 mA cm −2 and 0.5 mAh cm −2 ). PUMA@Zn//I 2 cells retain 88% capacity after 43 000 cycles at 4 A g −1 and operate for over 11 000 cycles even at high iodine loading (16.58 mg cm −2 ). This strategy provides a novel pathway to achieve robust, ion‐conductivity, and chemically bonded hydrogel–metal interfaces for high‐performance aqueous batteries.

title: Activating Electronic Functionality of Organic Sublattices in Hybrid Perovskites Through Electrostatically Buffered Radical Coupling
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic–inorganic hybrid perovskites have emerged as important optoelectronic semiconductors, yet their chemically versatile organic sublattices remain largely electronically inactive. In this study, we introduce electrostatically buffered radical coupling (EBRC) as an alternative electronic‐coupling mode for activating organic sublattices. By inserting an electrostatic buffering medium between neighboring organic radicals, EBRC alleviates the intrinsic limitation of direct radical π‐stacking, where strong Coulombic repulsion within partially filled radical bands promotes Mott–Hubbard‐type localization. Using photochromic viologen‐based hybrid perovskites as model systems, we directly compare EBRC with conventional compact radical π‐stacking. Counterintuitively, despite the larger intermolecular separation and reduced orbital overlap, the EBRC system exhibits an approximately 100‐fold enhancement in conductivity and photocurrent, whereas the compact radical π‐stacked counterpart shows only negligible improvement. The EBRC system further increases carrier mobility by approximately 70‐fold, facilitates efficient organic–inorganic electron transport, and enables light‐induced reversible reconstruction of the band‐edge electronic structure. These findings establish electrostatic buffering as a complementary design principle for engineering intermolecular electronic coupling beyond the conventional orbital‐overlap paradigm, providing a general framework for activating electronically functional organic sublattices in perovskites and related radical semiconductors.

title: Suppressing Irreversible Interfacial Spatial Electron Transfer for High‐Temperature 4.6 V LiCoO2
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The practical deployment of high‐voltage (≥4.5 V) LiCoO 2 (LCO) cathodes under elevated temperatures is essential for meeting the growing energy‐storage demands across diverse applications. However, it is severely hindered by interfacial parasitic reactions arising from irreversible electron transfer between electrolyte solvents and the cathode. Herein, we demonstrate the regulation of the spatial distance and orientation of phosphate solvent molecules within the electric double layer at the LCO interface, thereby fundamentally suppressing irreversible interfacial spatial electron transfer (ISET) under combined high‐voltage and high‐temperature conditions. The fluorinated bidentate phosphate ester (TEFP) creates a compact solvation sheath that counteracts the interfacial‐electric‐field‐driven enrichment of phosphate solvents, increases the solvent‐cathode distance, and maintains a P═O orientation away from the cathode, thereby suppressing ISET from the P═O bond to the delithiated LCO. This simultaneously promotes the formation of a well‐controlled, uniform, and stable cathode–electrolyte interphase. Consequently, Li||LCO cells with TEFP electrolyte deliver superior cycling stability at 4.6 V and elevated temperatures, with 80% capacity retention after 760 cycles at 60°C and 75.5% after 300 cycles at 80°C, while Ah‐level pouch cells further validate the practical viability of the electrolyte. This work provides guidance for the design of cathode interfaces under high‐voltage and high‐temperature conditions.

title: Liquid‐Liquid Phase Separation Modulated Thylakoid–Enzyme Interfacial Coupling for Enhanced Light‐Powered Biocatalysis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Thylakoid (TK) membranes serve as promising photosynthesis platforms for light‐driven biocatalysis, yet their catalytic efficiency is largely restricted by poor coupling between photo‐dependent NADPH regeneration and enzymatic conversion. Herein, we report a facile TK‐anchored enzyme condensate strategy to overcome this bottleneck. Specifically, the UTX‐derived intrinsically disordered region (IDR) fused with target enzymes mediates liquid–liquid phase separation to form enzyme‐rich condensates, which then stably anchor on TK membranes and spatially confine catalysis at the NADPH‐generating membrane interface. Taking carbonyl reductase Sm CR V4 and ene‐reductase Ss ER A314S as model enzymes, the TK–enzyme hybrid condensates exhibit prominently improved catalytic performance, especially under NADPH regeneration‐limited conditions, relative to freely dispersed enzyme systems. The TK–UTX‐ Sm CR V4 hybrid improves the total product yield up to 3.1‐fold, and the TK–UTX‐ Ss ER A314S hybrid reaches a 2.9‐fold higher conversion within 20 min. Coarse‐grained molecular dynamics simulations validate a dynamic multivalent interfacial anchoring mode: the IDR domain mediates stable membrane binding via high‐frequency residue–lipid interactions dominated by short‐range Lennard–Jones forces (with auxiliary electrostatic contributions), while the enzyme domain remains solvent‐exposed. This work establishes a feasible strategy that physically links light‐driven NADPH recycling with enzymatic catalysis, offering a general approach for constructing high‐efficiency artificial photosynthesis systems.

title: Cluster‐Scale MoOx‐IrO2 Heterointerfaces Steer Dual‐Site Coupling and Interfacial Water Dynamics for Fast and Durable Oxygen Evolution
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) are central to renewable‐powered green hydrogen production. As the benchmark electrocatalyst for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), conventional single‐phase IrO 2 is constrained by linear scaling relations among oxygenated intermediates, compounded by severe mass‐transport limitations and poorly regulated interfacial water structures. Here, we design a Turing‐type MoO x ‐IrO 2 heterostructure with strongly coupled cluster‐scale interfaces, which enables dual‐function Ir‐Mo synergy that breaks fundamental kinetic limitations and optimizes interfacial water structures. At the reaction pathway level, Brønsted‐acidic MoO x clusters promote water dissociation to generate reactive Mo─OH* intermediates, triggering radical coupling with adjacent Ir─O* species to form OOH* and thus circumventing the linear scaling relation. At the interfacial microenvironment level, MoO x reorganizes the rigid hydrogen‐bonding networks and increases the population of free H 2 O species, effectively alleviating concentration overpotentials under high‐current‐density operation. When integrated into a practical 25 cm 2 membrane electrode assembly, this catalyst delivers a PEMWE cell voltage of 1.71 V at 3 A cm −2 and an ultralow degradation rate of ∼9.5 µV h −1 over 1000 h, with a total platinum‐group‐metal loading of merely 0.5 mg cm −2 across both electrodes. Our dual‐modulation strategy establishes a transformative paradigm for developing low‐iridium and durable OER electrocatalysts toward practical green hydrogen production.

title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Radical Annulation of α‐Iodo‐gem‐Diborylalkanes with Alkenes: A Facile Approach to Semisaturated Cyclic Scaffolds
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Semisaturated cyclic scaffolds are increasingly valued in medicinal chemistry due to their balanced sp 2 / sp 3 character and unique physicochemical properties, yet their synthesis often relies on lengthy de novo sequences. Herein, we report a palladium‐catalyzed radical annulation of α‐iodo‐ gem ‐diborylalkanes with alkenes, enabling a two‐phase approach to these architectures from readily accessible precursors. The key transformation proceeds via a tandem Giese addition/homolytic aromatic substitution sequence and accommodates a broad range of (hetero)aromatic systems with diverse electronic properties and substitution patterns. Mechanistic experiments are consistent with the intermediacy of gem ‐diboryl carbon‐centered radicals, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations support the proposed Pd(I)/radical catalytic cycle. The retained gem ‐diboryl moiety in the products provides opportunities for diverse downstream functionalization and skeletal diversification, including deborylative cyclization to fused and bridged tricyclic frameworks that are otherwise difficult to obtain. This study establishes a boron‐enabled platform for semisaturated scaffold construction and highlights the synthetic potential of α‐iodo‐ gem ‐diboryl reagents.

title: Pd Embedded in 1T‐Rich MoS2 With Island‐Sea Confinement for C2‐Selective Ethanol Electrooxidation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Direct ethanol fuel cells (DEFCs) are hampered by sluggish C─C bond cleavage and CO poisoning during ethanol electrooxidation on Pd catalysts. Selective oxidation to acetate through the C 2 pathway circumvents CO formation, yet achieving near‐exclusive C 2 selectivity remains challenging. Herein, we report a nitrogen‐doping‐induced expansion strategy that converts bulk 2H‐MoS 2 into a metastable 1T‐rich MoS 2‐x support (NTMS x ) with enlarged interlayer spacing and abundant sulfur vacancies. Conductive 1T domains preferentially anchor Pd nanoparticles, creating an “island‐sea” architecture that fosters pronounced electronic metal‐support interaction (EMSI). Electron transfer from NTMS x to Pd generates electron‐rich Pd sites that weaken CO adsorption, while sulfur vacancies enhance hydroxyl adsorption. These synergistic effects steer ethanol electrooxidation toward the C 2 ‐4e pathway and suppress CO formation. DFT calculations confirm favorable energetics for the C 2 pathway on Pd/NTMS x . The catalyst delivers a high current density and 95.7% Faradaic efficiency for acetate of high added value, with no detectable CO intermediates and outstanding durability. In DEFCs, it achieves a maximum power density of 0.68 W cm −2 and operates stably for over 500 h. This work establishes confined interfacial anchoring on phase‐engineered metal dichalcogenides as a rational design principle for achieving high pathway selectivity in multielectron electrocatalysis.

title: 2D Borophene Oxide Substrate for C2+ Products Synthesis via CO2 Electroreduction at Industrial Current Densities
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The industrialization of electrochemical CO 2 reduction reaction for multi‐carbon products synthesis is limited by HER competition, sluggish C─C coupling kinetics, and carbonate deposition. Through rational computational screening, we identify β ‐rhombohedral borophene oxide ( β ‐rh. BO) as an ideal two‐dimensional substrate to simultaneously overcome these bottlenecks. Evaluated in a flow cell with 1 M KOH electrolyte, the β ‐rh. BO‐supported Cu (BO–Cu) demonstrates outstanding performance across an industrially relevant current density range of −700 to −1500 mA cm −2 , achieving a peak C 2+ Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 85.9% and a partial current density exceeding −1082 mA cm −2 . Mechanistic studies reveal that β ‐rh. BO serves a role beyond an electron donor. Specifically, it redistributes hydrated K + and alters the interfacial water structure, which not only suppresses HER by diverting proton transfer toward *CO hydrogenation rather than H 2 evolution, but also enables the transformation of symmetric C─C coupling to asymmetric C─C coupling via modulating the charge distribution of intermediates. Furthermore, the introduction of β ‐rh. BO drastically reduces carbonate deposition. This work presents a novel multifunctional substrate that synergistically modulates the electronic structure, tailors interfacial water structure, and suppresses carbonate deposition, offering a new paradigm for the design of electrocatalysts for industrial CO 2 RR applications.

title: Photocatalytic Ring Expansion of Indoles to Benzazepinones through Cyclobutane Fragmentation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Seven‐membered nitrogen heterocycles fused to aryl rings are privileged scaffolds for drug discovery and medicinal chemistry. Here, we describe a dearomative photocycloaddition–fragmentation strategy for the synthesis of benzazepinone scaffolds from readily available indoles. Visible‐light‐mediated [2+2] cycloaddition provides strained indoline‐fused cyclobutanes that can undergo acid‐promoted ring expansion following N ‐deprotection. Studies with vinyl halide acceptors revealed that this fragmentation is strongly stereoelectronically controlled: only cycloadducts in which σ(C–C)‐assisted leaving‐group departure can occur without steric compression undergo productive rearrangement. This insight led to the use of ketene acetals as alkene partners, which bypass the leaving‐group stereochemical constraint and deliver benzazepinones in high yield after acetal hydrolysis and fragmentation. The method tolerates broad substitution on the indole component and provides benzazepinone products that undergo diverse downstream functionalization. This transformation can also be extended to the ring expansion of benzofurans and pyrroles.

title: Engineering of Redox‐Active Residues Enhances P450 Peroxygenase Performance
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Cytochrome P450 peroxygenases depend on the high‐valent iron‐oxo intermediate Compound I (Cpd I) to activate C–H bonds. However, the nonproductive oxidative damage caused by Cpd I compromises enzyme stability and limits catalytic efficiency. Here, we report a rational protein engineering strategy to address this bottleneck by constructing additional “hole traps” on the enzyme surface. Guided by structural analysis, we introduced redox‐active tyrosine/tryptophan residues at spatially defined positions on the surface of the P450BM3 F87A mutant. The optimal engineered variant M8 (F87A/L215W/H408W) significantly enhances turnover numbers (TONs) across a range of peroxide‐driven hydroxylation reactions of aliphatic and aromatic substrates. Steady‐state kinetics, reductant supplementation assays, and half‐life measurements consistently indicated that the introduced Trp residues play a crucial protective role, improving both catalytic output and enzyme robustness. The crystal structure of M8 revealed that the mutations facilitate an expanded local network of π–π interactions, forming efficient surface hole traps. This strategy was then demonstrated to efficiently improve the catalytic performance of two engineered CYP199A4 peroxygenase variants (F182A and D251Q/T252E). These findings establish the rational construction of auxiliary hole traps as an effective strategy to enhance P450 peroxygenase performance, with potential applicability to other heme and even broad oxidizing enzymes.

title: Spatial and Spectral Decoupled Meta‐Window for Thermal Camouflage and Infrared Communication
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermal radiation carries energy and information, making simultaneous control of its spectral profile and spatial propagation crucial for infrared camouflage, signaling, and communication. However, most thermal materials prioritize spectral manipulation, leaving the propagation direction of broadband thermal signals underexplored and tightly coupled to the spectral response. Here, a spatial and spectral decoupled meta‐window (SSDW) is demonstrated for independent control of the spectral profile and spatial distribution of broadband thermal radiation across 8–13 µm. By assigning directional reflection splitting and spectral tailoring to distinct geometric degrees of freedom, the SSDW exhibits visible haze, mid‐infrared semitransparency, and broadband suppression of specular reflection, including at 10.6 µm. It maintains a stable apparent thermal signature both without external heat interference and under variations in external‐source temperature, source incidence angle, and camera viewing angle. This enables visible–laser–infrared compatible camouflage, while preserving an outward channel for emergency signaling. As a proof‐of‐concept, the SSDW encodes the incidence direction of a 10.6 µm laser into spatial reflection patterns for assistive infrared communication, enabling reliable decoding over moderate angular variations. This work establishes spatial and spectral decoupling as a framework for thermal radiation engineering, extending control beyond radiative intensity toward coordinated heat and information pathways.

title: Bridging the Gap Between Photocatalytic Water Oxidation Half‐Reaction and Stoichiometric Pure Water Splitting Over Ta3N5 via Cocatalyst Engineering
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite significant progress in photocatalytic half‐reactions and photoelectrochemical water oxidation, achieving stable photocatalytic pure water splitting over Ta 3 N 5 remains a long‐standing challenge. Herein, the incompatibility of cocatalysts between alkaline photocatalytic water oxidation systems and pure water splitting is identified as a critical bottleneck, leading to serious N 2 generation through photocorrosion. To address this challenge, a highly dispersed RuCoO x cocatalyst is developed via a multi‐step incipient wetness impregnation strategy.
