title: Macrocycle Size-Controlled Dynamic and Static Chirality in Donor–Acceptor [2]Catenanes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Chiral [2]catenanes, a prominent class of mechanically interlocked molecules (MIMs), can exhibit either static or dynamic mechanostereochemistry. Controlling these mechanostereochemical states without altering the covalent connectivity, however, remains challenging. Herein, we report a series of chiral [2]catenanes derived from ExBox and cycloparaphenyleneperylene (CPPP), whose dynamic behavior is altered by the size of the CPPP macrocycle. We identified a sharp, size-dependent threshold: The conformational stereogenic unit of [7]CPPP is kinetically locked, whereas those of [8]CPPP and [9]CPPP are dynamic at room temperature. This conformational stereochemistry strongly biases the co-conformational stereochemistry in the catenane, effectively resulting in a single dominant diastereomer. This effective coupling of the two stereogenic units allows the conformational stereochemistry to be biased by the ion pairing of the interlocked cationic ring with a chiral anion. This research highlights the potential of mechanically interlocked architectures for controlling the dynamic mechanostereochemistry.

title: Molecular Architecture of Covalent Adaptable Network Additives Governs Their Integration into Melt-Processed Polyamide 6
abstract: Abstract Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) are predominantly developed as bulk thermoset matrices, while their use as dynamically crosslinked functional phases within melt-processed thermoplastics remains largely unexplored. Here, phosphorus-containing CANs (P-CANs) with systematically varied molecular architectures are employed as macromolecular additives in polyamide 6 (PA6) to establish relationships between network structure, dynamic response, dispersion, retention, and melt processability. Transitioning from a rigid small-molecule-derived network to flexible polyphosphonate architectures shifted the glass-transition temperature from 160 to –5 °C and markedly altered stress relaxation and deformation under processing conditions. These architecture-dependent differences translated directly into thermoplastic integration: the rigid P-CAN formed larger phosphorus-rich domains and exhibited greater phosphorus retention, whereas the most flexible network appeared more uniformly dispersed, lowered processing resistance, and promoted shear-thinning behavior. The resulting balance between dispersion and retention enabled kilogram-scale twin-screw compounding and continuous film extrusion of homogeneous PA6 composites containing 5–10 wt % flexible P-CAN. Despite low final phosphorus contents (∼0.25–0.60 wt %), incorporation of the P-CANs increased limiting oxygen index, promoted char formation, and reduced microscale heat release. These results demonstrate that CAN molecular architecture provides a tunable design parameter for controlling the integration and functional performance of dynamically crosslinked polymeric additives in melt-processed thermoplastics.

title: Dual-Microstructure Configuration Design Enabling Highly Sensitive Biotemplated Flexible Capacitive Pressure Sensors
abstract: Abstract Flexible capacitive pressure sensors (FCPSs) that resolve subtle pressure are central to soft robotics and human health monitoring. Their sensitivity is affected by microstructures incorporated at the interface between the electrode and dielectric layers, but fabricating fine artificial microstructures typically requires costly techniques. Biological templates offer a cost-effective way to form these microstructures, yet biotemplated FCPSs have remained limited in sensitivity. Efforts to improve sensitivity have predominantly focused on microstructure geometries, whereas the microstructure configuration in the sensor has not been well-studied. Here, we establish design insights for microstructure configurations through simplified computational analysis, revealing that amplifying the effective interelectrode distance variation rate and effective permittivity variation rate within the structured region is the key to enhancing overall sensitivity. Following this insight, we propose a dual-microstructure configuration that increases the air fraction within the structured region, leading to the amplified effective permittivity variation rate. Both computational and experimental assessments demonstrate that the dual-microstructure configuration outperforms conventional ones in sensitivity, with the fabricated sensor achieving the highest sensitivity of 4.3 kPa–1 among all the reported biotemplated FCPSs using the same dielectric materials (Table S1), along with a fast response/recovery time of 46/20 ms, a low detection limit of 1.2 Pa, and stable operation over 7500 cycles. These performance attributes enable the sensor for applications in robotic hand tactile sensing for soft objects and real-time physiological signal monitoring. Consequently, the proposed dual-microstructure configuration offers a generalizable pathway to enhance the sensitivity of biotemplated FCPSs, promoting the development of high-performance, cost-effective flexible pressure sensors.

title: IMAN: An Integrated Colorimetric Sensor for Direct Detection of PD-L1 on Extracellular Vesicles in Lung Cancer Diagnosis
abstract: Abstract Lung cancer is a leading cause of cancer mortality, yet early diagnosis remains difficult, highlighting the need for sensitive, noninvasive methods. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) and their surface proteins (e.g., PD-L1) are promising biomarkers; nevertheless, current EV detection requires time-consuming purification, sophisticated instrumentation, and long measurement protocols, resulting in high expenses and operational difficulties. This study developed an integrated colorimetric sensor, IMAN, based on a strategy of “Immunomagnetic Microbeads (IM) capture + Aptamer(Apt) recognition + Nanozyme (N) catalysis”. IMAN employs magnetic beads modified with antibodies against CD9 and CD81 to directly capture EVs from serum, eliminating the need for time-consuming prior isolation; combined with a one-step colorimetric readout, the entire workflow can be completed with only ∼40 min of hands-on time, requiring no complex instrumentation. The PD-L1 protein on the EV surface is specifically recognized by a nanoparticle-bound nucleic acid aptamer. Signal generation is achieved through the catalytic oxidation of 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) by a platinum-gold bimetallic nanozyme (Pt@Au). The facile IMAN colorimetric method demonstrated a relatively broad dynamic range (107–1010 particles/mL), high specificity (unaffected by 100 pg/mL soluble PD-L1 in serum), and reproducibility (relative standard deviation, RSD = 9.1%). title: Structured Filler-Enabled Pore-Interface Engineering in Polydimethylsiloxane for Passive Radiative Cooling
abstract: Abstract Passive radiative cooling (PRC) materials require efficient solar scattering, high thermal emissivity, and mechanical compliance, yet constructing hierarchical pore-interface architectures that simultaneously enhance particle scattering, interface scattering, and flexibility within a single polymer system remains challenging. Here, we report a structured filler-induced pore-interface engineering strategy for flexible PRC films. Carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) and silane-modified SiO2 nanoparticles were electrostatically assembled into a spatially organized CMC@SiO2 filler, which simultaneously acts as a scattering unit and a pore-forming scaffold. Upon incorporation into polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), the structured filler induces hierarchical pore architectures with SiO2-decorated pore walls, generating coupled particle-scattering and pore-interface scattering pathways. The Finite-Difference Time-Domain simulations reveal that the multiscale architecture broadens solar scattering across the 0.25–2.5 μm range through enhanced refractive-index contrast and multiple-scattering effects. Benefiting from the coupled contribution of SiO2 scattering centers, hierarchical pore interfaces, and the intrinsic mid-infrared (MIR) emissivity of PDMS, the resulting film achieves a solar reflectivity of 94.6% and a MIR emissivity of 95.2%. The film delivers a maximum sub-ambient cooling of 7.1 °C under direct sunlight. Building energy simulations further predict an average annual cooling-energy reduction of 10.4% across representative climate zones in China. This work establishes a structured filler-enabled hierarchical pore-interface engineering strategy that integrates scattering enhancement, porous architectures, and polymer flexibility, offering a general route toward scalable and high-performance PRC materials.

title: Sustainable Thermoplastic Thermal Interface Adhesive Derived from Poly(lipoic acid) and Boron Nitride for Efficient Electronic Thermal Management
abstract: Abstract The escalating power density of electronics demands thermal interface materials (TIMs) that simultaneously offer high thermal conductivity, strong adhesion, and environmental sustainability. Conventional thermally conductive adhesives (TCAs) face inherent trade-offs among these properties, often relying on non-recyclable thermosets. Here, we present a sustainable thermoplastic TCA composed of a poly(lipoic acid) (polyLA)-based dynamic polymer matrix integrated with polyvinylpyrrolidone-modified hexagonal boron nitride (BN@PVP). The polyLA matrix incorporates catechol moieties and reversible Fe3+-carboxyl/catechol coordination bonds, creating a dynamically reconfigurable network. This design yields an adhesive (LD50Fe100) with high toughness (1.52 MJ m–3), and strong lap shear adhesion (884 kPa on PMMA and 1210 kPa on steel). The dynamic bonds enable room-temperature self-healing (93.1% efficiency) and robust recyclability. At a BN@PVP loading of 40 wt %, the composite (BN@LD50Fe100) achieves a thermal conductivity of 1.2 W m–1 K–1 while maintaining enhanced mechanical properties. LED chip heat dissipation experiments demonstrate a 4 °C lower operating temperature compared to devices without a TIM, with stable thermal performance over multiple cycles. This work provides a promising material strategy to overcome the traditional trade-offs in TCAs, offering a path toward repairable, reusable, and efficient thermal management solutions for advanced electronic packaging.

title: Bamboo-Inspired Homogeneous Porous Aerogel via Gas Foaming Assisted by Freeze-Drying for High-Sensitivity Flexible Pressure Sensors
abstract: Abstract Flexible piezoresistive sensors are pivotal in personalized healthcare. However, simultaneously achieving high sensitivity and a broad linear range remains a formidable challenge owing to rapid structural densification of porous materials. Inspired by the multiscale composite structure of bamboo, this study addresses the existing challenge by proposing a novel MXene aerogel sensor, reinforced by compounding cellulose nanofiber (CNF) Several instances of CNFs (which were introduced during copyediting) have been reverted back to CNF, consistent with our original submission where the abbreviation was defined as cellulose nanofiber (CNF). Corresponding grammatical adjustments are made to match this usage. This change only standardizes the abbreviation and does not alter any scientific content. and bamboo cellulose. By leveraging a uniform conductive network constructed on CNF (simulating bamboo parenchyma cells to disperse the vascular bundles) and the supporting effect of the bamboo cellulose skeleton (mimicking vascular bundles to provide support), premature collapse is effectively resisted. Moreover, inspired by the hollow cell cavity structure of bamboo, a stable porous architecture is constructed via gas foaming and freeze-drying, enabling it to effectively reconcile the inherent trade-off between sensitivity and the detection range. The sensor exhibits a high sensitivity of 148.29 kPa–1 (0–15 kPa) and a wide effective working range extending up to 100 kPa. This superior electromechanical performance enables the precise detection of full-spectrum physiological signals ranging from subtle pulse waveforms to large-scale joint movements and facilitates assistive rehabilitation for post-stroke finger therapy via human–computer interaction. Augmented by a support vector machine algorithm, the sensor has a wireless sleep monitoring capability and achieves a high classification accuracy of 96.5% in identifying distinct breathing states. The proposed sensor demonstrates significant application potential in next-generation intelligent home health management systems.

title: Interfacial Kinetic Matching in Amorphous Fe2O3/Crystalline Cu2O Enables Efficient Nitrate-To-Ammonia Electrosynthesis
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical nitrate (NO3–) reduction to ammonia (NH3) is a promising route for simultaneous nitrate remediation and sustainable NH3 synthesis, yet remains challenged by sluggish multistep hydrogenation kinetics. Here, we report an amorphous Fe2O3/crystalline Cu2O catalyst (a-Fe2O3/c-Cu2O), in which ultrasmall Cu2O nanocrystallites are uniformly dispersed in an amorphous Fe2O3 matrix. The resulting a-Fe2O3/c-Cu2O interface induces strong electronic interaction and complementary catalytic functions. The pH-dependent potential analysis shows that a-Fe2O3/c-Cu2O maintains a highly alkaline interfacial microenvironment, while stepwise kinetic measurements reveal favorable kinetic matching between NO3– activation and subsequent NO2– hydrogenation. In situ spectroscopic studies reveal a tandem catalytic pathway in which NO3– is first activated on c-Cu2O to form NO2–, followed by transfer to adjacent a-Fe2O3 sites for hydrogenation to NH3. Consequently, a-Fe2O3/c-Cu2O achieves an NH3 Faradaic efficiency of 92.4% and an NH3 yield rate of 6.25 mmol h–1 mg–1, and sustains stable operation for 100 h in a membrane electrode assembly electrolyzer. This work offers a viable strategy for promoting nitrate-to-ammonia electrosynthesis through amorphous/crystalline interfacial engineering.

title: Synergistic Coordination Regulation and Nanofiller-Guided Ion Transport in a Polyacrylamide Gel Electrolyte for Highly Reversible Aqueous Zn Metal Anodes
abstract: Abstract Despite their safety and cost advantages, aqueous zinc-ion batteries remain limited by the instability of Zn metal anodes, including nonuniform deposition, dendrite growth, and parasitic reactions. A PAM/CMC-Na/CNTs (PCC) hydrogel electrolyte is constructed by incorporating sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC-Na) and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) into a polyacrylamide (PAM) matrix. The –COO– and –OH groups of CMC-Na regulate the local coordination environment of Zn2+ and suppress water-related side reactions, while CNTs reinforce the gel network and improve interfacial contact. PCC exhibits an ionic conductivity of 24.16 mS cm–1 and an apparent Zn2+ transference number of 0.791. These transport characteristics, together with interfacial analyses, are consistent with more uniform Zn deposition. Zn//Zn symmetric cells cycle stably for over 2300 h at 1 mA cm–2 with an areal capacity of 1 mAh cm–2 and for approximately 550 h at 5 mA cm–2 with a capacity of 5 mAh cm–2. Zn//Cu cells achieve an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.94%, while Zn//MnO2 full cells retain 81.64% capacity after 700 cycles at 1 A g–1. A high-loading Zn//MnO2 pouch cell further demonstrates favorable energy-storage performance. This work presents a strategy for designing hydrogel electrolytes that integrate coordination regulation, homogenized ion transport, and mechanical robustness.

title: Hierarchical Functionalized Lignin Interfaces Regulate Water Transport in Low-Coating-Content Bio-Based Polyurethane-Coated Urea
abstract: Abstract Bio-based polyurethane coatings are promising for controlled-release fertilizers, but their release performance at low coating contents is often limited by rapid surface wetting and water transport through the coating membrane. Here, we constructed a hierarchical lignin-based interface on castor-oil-derived polyurethane-coated urea to regulate water–coating interactions. Lignin micro/nanospheres were sequentially functionalized with polydopamine and octadecyltrichlorosilane and introduced at the outer polyurethane interface during the final coating stage. Thermodynamic calculations and spectroscopic analyses were consistent with interfacial chemical coupling between polydopamine-associated functional groups and residual isocyanate groups in the polyurethane coating. The resulting interface increased the apparent water contact angle from 87.4° to 157.2°, weakened the calculated adsorption of water, and reduced water-vapor permeability through the coating. Under a nominal total coating-material input of approximately 3 wt %, the cumulative nitrogen release within 10 days decreased from 56% for bio-based polyurethane-coated urea (BCU) to 20% for OTS-LMNPs@PDA-modified bio-based controlled-release urea (SBCU), while the time required to reach 80% nitrogen release increased from 20 to 49 days. This enhanced release performance was associated with reduced surface wetting, lower water affinity, and slower water transport across the modified coating, which collectively delayed water penetration, urea dissolution, and subsequent nitrogen diffusion. These results demonstrate that lignin-based interfacial modification provides an effective strategy for regulating water transport and improving the controlled-release performance of low-coating-content bio-based polyurethane fertilizers.

title: An Organic–Inorganic Hybrid Memristor with Trap-Assisted Hopping for Synaptic Plasticity and Artificial Nociceptor
abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic hardware demands artificial synaptic devices that mimic biological synapses. Achieving multifunctional emulation of synaptic plasticity and nociceptive behavior in a single, highly stable, low-power device remains a major challenge. In this report, zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnONP) are synthesized via a surfactant-assisted sol–gel method. These are incorporated into an organic small-molecule matrix of 6,13-bis(triisopropylsilylethynyl)pentacene (TP) to fabricate a solution-processed organic–inorganic hybrid memristor. title: Magnetic Fe/Cu Metal–Organic Frameworks-Derived Trilayer Cathode for Enhanced Enrofloxacin Degradation in Heterogeneous Electro-Fenton via Synergistic Radical and Nonradical Pathways
abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous electro-Fenton (HEF) technology represents a promising eco-friendly strategy for wastewater remediation. However, sluggish Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling and reliance on a single hydroxyl radical (•OH) pathway limit its overall catalytic efficiency and oxidant utilization. Herein, a bifunctional trilayer cathode (Fe8Cu2@C-GF/ACF) was fabricated by integrating activated carbon fiber (ACF) with a magnetic Fe/Cu metal–organic frameworks-derived layer grown on graphite felt. This architecture spatially couples H2O2 electrogeneration with immediate activation, maximizing the effective utilization of generated oxidants. Furthermore, Cu incorporation thermodynamically accelerates Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling. The bimetallic synergy facilitates the simultaneous generation of radical (•OH) and nonradical (1O2) species. Quenching and EPR analyses confirmed these dual pathways collectively accelerate enrofloxacin (ENRO) degradation. The system achieves excellent mineralization across a broad initial pH range (3.0 to 9.0). Crucially, effective operation at neutral pH eliminates the need for chemical adjustment. Specifically, treating 100 mg L−1 ENRO at initial pH 7.0 and 18 mA cm−2 yielded a 75.6% mineralization degree. Degradation intermediates were elucidated via DFT calculations and UPLC-QqQ-MS analysis. Finally, the cathode exhibits high stability and low metal leaching. Its intrinsic magnetic recoverability prevents secondary solid waste and promotes practical material reuse for sustainable water treatment.

title: Dynamic Energy-Dissipating Interface Design Reconciles Thermal Performance with Interfacial Reliability
abstract: Abstract Highly filled thermal interface materials (TIMs) are essential for reliable heat dissipation in high-power electronics, yet restricted polymer chain mobility and reduced interfacial conformability make it difficult to achieve high thermal conductivity, strong adhesion, and crack-growth resistance simultaneously. We propose a dynamic energy-dissipating interface (DEDI) strategy that coordinates favorable interfacial affinity, stable chemical anchoring, and dynamic bulk energy dissipation to improve interfacial stability and crack resistance in highly filled TIMs. γ-Methacryloxypropyl trimethoxysilane (γ-MPS) provides stable chemical anchoring at the substrate interface, while urethane-associated polar interactions contribute to favorable interfacial affinity. Reversible disulfide and hydrogen-bond interactions within the bulk network promote deformation accommodation and mechanical energy dissipation. Surface-modified Al2O3/ZnO hybrid fillers form a multiscale network that provides efficient heat-transfer pathways. The resulting PSM-60-1.2 exhibits a thermal conductivity of 3.88 W·m−1·K−1, an adhesion strength of 4.25 MPa, and an adhesion energy of 3080.04 J·m−2. Combined experimental and finite-element analyses support coordinated interfacial stabilization, bulk energy dissipation, and enhanced thermomechanical deformation accommodation. After 100 thermal shock cycles between −40 and 150 °C, PSM-60-1.2 shows a 6.0 °C increase in maximum steady-state temperature, compared with 16.2 °C for the commercial thermally conductive adhesive, with less interfacial cracking and low-viscosity liquid infiltration. The DEDI design offers a molecular strategy for combining high thermal conductivity, high adhesion energy, and long-term thermomechanical reliability in highly filled TIMs.

title: Three-Dimensional-Printed Lithium-Doped Conductive Carbon@Hydroxyapatite Scaffolds for Coordinated Neurovascular-Osseous Regeneration
abstract: Abstract The repair of critical-sized bone defects remains a formidable clinical challenge, where coordinated neurovascular reconstruction is important for effective bone regeneration. Accordingly, this study aimed to develop a three-dimensional (3D)-printed hydroxyapatite (HAp) scaffold integrating a polydopamine (PDA)-derived conductive carbon interface with Li+ release, and to evaluate its neural-, vascular-, and osteogenic-related effects in vitro and its bone-regenerative performance in vivo. A lithium-containing, hydrothermally carbonized HAp scaffold (HAp@C/Li) was fabricated through 3D printing, Li+-assisted dopamine coating, and hydrothermal carbonization. Material characterization confirmed a PDA-derived carbon coating with measurable local surface conductivity and Li+ release characterized by an early release phase followed by a gradual plateau. In vitro experimental results revealed that HAp@C/Li possessed excellent cytocompatibility. It effectively promoted neurite outgrowth of dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons, migration and tube formation of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs), as well as osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). In vivo evaluation in a rat femoral condyle defect model showed favorable bone repair, collagen deposition, vascular remodeling, and neural-associated tissue responses, with significantly higher BMD at 8 weeks, whereas BV/TV did not differ significantly from that of the HAp group. Collectively, these results indicate that the HAp@C/Li scaffold provides a promising therapeutic strategy for the clinical repair of critical-sized bone defects.

title: Vicinal Functional-Group Engineering in Defect-Engineered MOFs for One-Step Ethylene Purification
abstract: Abstract The development of C2H6-selective adsorbents offers a promising strategy for energy-efficient C2H4 purification from C2H6/C2H4 mixtures. However, the similar physicochemical properties of C2H6 and C2H4 make it challenging to achieve preferential adsorption of C2H6. Herein, we propose a vicinal functional-group engineering strategy to construct C2H6-recognition domains, enabling efficient one-step C2H4 purification from C2H6/C2H4 mixtures. The adjacent functional groups on the modulators are introduced close to the defect sites of MOFs, constructing synergistic electrostatic-confinement microenvironments for C2H6 recognition. The fluorinated-defective MOF (UiO-66-(CF3)2) exhibits C2H6 preferential adsorption with an uptake of 2.2 mmol/g at 298 K and 100 kPa. Breakthrough experiments further confirm the dynamic separation performance of UiO-66-(CF3)2, achieving high-purity C2H4 (>99.99 %) with a productivity of 12.67 L/kg. Theoretical calculations further reveal that the adjacent functional groups in the ligands would induce electrostatic potential redistribution and confined pore structures, strengthening C2H6 adsorption on defective MOF over C2H4. This work establishes a vicinal functional-group engineering strategy for constructing synergistic electrostatic-confinement microenvironments toward C2H6 recognition in MOFs.

title: High-Performance SrLiAl3N4:Eu2+ Red Phosphor via Alloy Precursor Synthesis for Laser-Driven and Wide-Gamut Displays
abstract: Abstract In this work, the alloy-precursor solid-state synthesis strategy (AS-method) is employed to fabricate high-performance SrLiAl3N4:Eu2+ phosphors. This approach effectively suppresses the oxidation of Eu2+ to Eu3+ compared to conventional solid-state synthesis (S-method). The resultant optimization of the local structure not only enhances the structural rigidity but also modulates the surrounding chemical pressure at different activator sites. This site-selective regulation leads to spectral narrowing and a blue shift in the emission. The optimized phosphor exhibits an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 52.38%, a value that ranks among the highest reported for the SLA-based phosphors. Furthermore, it demonstrates an ultrahigh saturation threshold of 90.69 W/mm2 under blue laser excitation, surpassing most reported red phosphors. When applied in white LEDs, it achieves 104% of the NTSC color gamut. Thus, this phosphor indicates great potential for applications in both laser-driven and high-color-gamut displays.

title: Synergistic Interfacial Engineering in V2C MXene Heterostructures for Enhanced Nano-aluminum Reactivity
abstract: Abstract Nano-aluminum (nano-Al) is a high-energy-density material with exceptional reactivity, making it promising for aerospace and military applications. Reducing particle size increases the active surface area and interfacial mass diffusion, but intrinsic agglomeration and dense alumina shells hinder diffusion. Conventional additives often reduce reactivity. Here, we modulate nano-Al interfacial diffusion through synergistic interactions in a V2C MXene heterostructure. The self-assembly of nano-Al on MXene suppresses agglomeration, while fluorine-containing terminations etch the alumina shells. The heterostructure also forms metal oxide contact layers that promote solid-phase thermite reactions. These effects increase the peak heat flow in air to 107.6 W g−1, 3.5 times that of pristine nano-Al. Solid-phase reactions complete energy release before Al melting, minimizing energy loss. The composite shows larger flame areas and a lower minimum ignition concentration (≥5 wt %). Adjusting the heating temperature reduces the total combustion duration by 88.9% and increases the dynamic pressure. This versatile fabrication process enables tunable performance for diverse operational environments.

title: Controlled Interfacial Electronic Coupling in Chemical Vapor Deposition-Grown WSe2 Monolayers on Au(111)
abstract: Abstract We report on the controlled growth and interface engineering of high-quality WSe2 monolayers on Au(111) using ambient-pressure chemical vapor deposition (CVD) combined with comprehensive surface-sensitive characterization in ultrahigh vacuum (UHV). The as-grown films exhibit a selenium buffer layer, which enables the formation of a weakly coupled WSe2 phase at the metal interface, as revealed by scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and low-energy electron diffraction (LEED). Annealing in UHV removes the selenium buffer layer and leads to the emergence of a pronounced moiré superstructure and a transition toward a strongly coupled WSe2 phase. Furthermore, this transformation is accompanied by pronounced modifications of the electronic structure, including phase-dependent changes in the valence band structure observed by angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy (ARPES), a hybridization-induced metallization measured by scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS), and a significant decrease in the work function determined by field emission resonance (FER) and ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy (UPS). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm strong WSe2–Au hybridization and the presence of the mid-gap states for the strongly coupled phase, whereas the Se8 buffer layer weakens the interaction of WSe2 with Au, so that its electronic structure is close to that for the freestanding system. Our results demonstrate that growth-induced interface chemistry provides a powerful handle to tune the electronic coupling in WSe2/Au(111), establishing a direct link between interfacial structure and electronic properties in metal–transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) interfaces.

title: Improvement of Photocatalytic and Nanomechanical Properties of GaN Nanowires via Core-Shell Surface Modification
abstract: Abstract The practical implementation of photocatalytic water splitting for sustainable hydrogen production is largely limited by the efficiency of the oxygen evolution reaction at the photoanode. Gallium nitride is a promising material for photoanode fabrication, provided that suitable nanostructuring strategies are applied to enhance its efficiency and stability. Here, we report the functionalization of gallium nitride nanowires with a 5 nm-thick titanium dioxide layer of and a 10 nm biomimetic polydopamine coating, resulting in a 1.9-fold (190%) increase in the anodic photocurrent, as demonstrated by chronoamperometry. We provide a detailed explanation of this enhancement based on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and a series of optical studies. The observed decrease in photoluminescence intensity (60–90%) and shortening of carrier lifetimes from 0.17 to 0.07 ns correlate with the improved photocatalytic performance. Moreover, the 50% reduction in the band-to-band to defect emission ratio and the analysis of exciton recombination pathways show the role of defect-related and surface recombination processes in determining the photocatalytic activity of the nanowires. The enhanced photocatalytic performance is further attributed to shell deposition, which induces surface-state passivation, band realignment, and the quantum-confined Stark effect. Concurrently, changes in strain distribution are confirmed by increased heterogeneity of the GaN E2high phonon mode frequency distribution, expressed by an increase in the standard deviation from 0.09 up to 0.17 cm–1 and linewidth broadening from 3.2 up to 3.4 cm–1, as observed by Raman spectroscopy. Additionally, we show that the nanomechanical properties of the nanowires are significantly improved after shell deposition, by the elimination of pop-in events, enhanced elastic recovery, and an increase in Young’s modulus from 12 to 37 GPa. Finally, we point out opportunities for further optimization of similarly functionalized nanowire systems to achieve even higher efficiencies and support emerging applications.

title: Modelling and Emulation of Afferent-Like Excitatory–Inhibitory Spiking Using Ovonic Threshold Devices for Neuromorphic Oscillatory Computing
abstract: Abstract Spike-based computing has attracted increasing attention for efficient information processing, creating demand for neuromorphic hardware capable of generating and processing spikes. Ovonic threshold switching (OTS) devices are promising spiking neurons because their threshold-switching behavior and negative differential resistance enable compact spike-generation circuits, while their scalability supports dense integration. However, a circuit-level design framework linking defect dynamics with conduction behavior remains lacking. Here, we experimentally demonstrate an intensity-tuned artificial neuron based on a GeAsTe OTS device integrated with a resistor-capacitor (RC) circuit. The neuron shows a non-monotonic excitatory–self-inhibitory response with applied voltage, phenomenologically analogous to excitatory–inhibitory behavior in biological neurons. The spiking frequency initially increases and then decreases beyond an inflection voltage point. This transition arises intrinsically from competition between RC charging dynamics and conductive filament retention in the OTS device, rather than from a separate inhibitory pathway. The neuron achieves a spiking frequency of up to 1.6 MHz. The behavior is supported by simulations using a dynamical model for diffusive filament-based memristors, accounting for resistance changes from filament formation and rupture. Furthermore, a physics-informed compact SPICE model combining defect-state transitions and filament evolution reproduces OTS switching and predicts neuron dynamics under varying temperatures, internal resistances, and circuit conditions. Finally, circuit simulations of a coupled OTS neuron network demonstrate vertex coloring with phase convergence within approximately 5 μs, highlighting the potential of this framework for compact, energy-efficient brain-inspired computing.

title: Surface and Electronic-Structure Regulation of NiCrPt-LDH for Ampere-Level Methanol-Assisted Hydrogen Production in Alkaline Seawater
abstract: Abstract Substituting the anodic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) with the methanol oxidation reaction (MOR) provides an energy-saving route for alkaline seawater electrolysis, but it demands bifunctional electrodes that efficiently facilitate both anodic MOR and cathodic hydrogen evolution reactions (HER) in chloride-containing alkaline media. This work reports a surface and electronic-structure regulation strategy for a low-Pt (0.86 wt %) NiCrPt-LDH electrode constructed on nickel foam via a single-step hydrothermal route. The NiCrPt-LDH electrode integrates an open nanosheet framework, a defect-enriched metal–oxygen surface environment, and a super-hydrophilic/-aerophobic interface, which requires only 74, 146, and 228 mV to deliver 100, 500, and 1000 mA cm–2 for HER, respectively, with 1380 h of stability at 500 mA cm–2. Its Pt-mass-normalized HER activity is much higher than that of commercial Pt/C. For MOR in methanol-containing alkaline seawater, NiCrPt-LDH reaches 100 mA cm–2 under an applied potential of 1.401 V vs RHE. The NiCrPt-LDH (+) || NiCrPt-LDH (–) electrolyzer outputs 100 mA cm–2 at an operating voltage of 1.477 V, underscoring the potential of low-platinum, surface-engineered bifunctional LDH electrodes for methanol-assisted hydrogen production in alkaline seawater electrolysis.

title: High- k Gate Dielectrics for Organic Field-Effect Transistors: Interfacial Engineering, Performance Optimization, and Scalable Flexible Electronics
abstract: Abstract Organic field-effect transistors (OFETs) are promising platforms for flexible, wearable, biointegrated, and large-area electronics owing to their mechanical compliance, solution processability, low-temperature fabrication, and molecular tunability. However, their practical application requires low-voltage operation, low power consumption, high operational stability, and scalable manufacturing, which are strongly influenced by the gate dielectric and its interface with the organic semiconductor. High-k gate dielectrics can increase gate capacitance and enhance electrostatic control, enabling low-voltage operation. However, a higher dielectric constant does not necessarily lead to better device performance, as strong polarization, surface polarity, interfacial trapping, dipolardisorder, remote phonon scattering, leakage, ion migration, and dielectric–semiconductor incompatibility can impair charge transport and device reliability. This Review presents a performance-oriented and interface-centered overview of high-k gate dielectrics for OFETs. We first classify high-k dielectric systems into inorganic oxides, molecularly engineered polymers, organic–inorganic hybrids and composites, and all-organic composite/multilayer structures, highlighting their polarization mechanisms, advantages, limitations, and structure–property relationships. We then discuss how dielectric properties and interfaces affect carrier mobility, threshold voltage, switching characteristics, charge injection, leakage current, hysteresis, and operational stability. Particular attention is given to interface engineering strategies, including surface modification, buffer layers, multilayer architectures, molecular design, composite construction, and defect/passivation control. We further discuss long-term reliability under electrical, thermal, mechanical, and environmental stresses, as well as emerging dielectric systems, low-temperature and scalable fabrication, large-area uniformity, process integration, and commercialization challenges. Finally, we summarize key design considerations for balancing high capacitance, low leakage, interfacial compatibility, mechanical robustness, environmental stability, and scalable processability. By integrating dielectric design, interface engineering, device physics, reliability, and manufacturing, this Review provides guidelines for developing low-voltage, stable, and scalable OFETs for next-generation flexible electronics.

title: In Situ Activated Bi2WO6 Nanosheets with Fast-Response and Self-Bleaching Electrochromism for Automotive Antiglare Rearview Mirrors
abstract: Abstract Trailing vehicle headlight glare critically endangers nighttime driving safety, with electrochromic devices (ECDs) being the most promising solution. Nevertheless, commercial organic electrochromic materials face high cost and irreversible degradation, whereas inorganic alternatives exhibit slow response and severe memory effect, severely restricting their application in antiglare rearview mirrors. Herein, we report the electrochromic behavior of thin bismuth tungstate (T-BWO) nanosheets synthesized via a facile hydrothermal method. A unique in situ activation process is discovered, accompanied by (19.7 ± 1.8)% leaching of surface Bi atoms and a transient dark transition state, which endows the activated T-BWO with exceptional electrochromic performance: an ultralow working voltage window of –0.6/0.3 V, ultrafast coloration/bleaching times of (0.81 ± 0.06)/(0.55 ± 0.04) s, a high coloration efficiency of (148.3 ± 7.8) cm2 C–1, and reasonably fast self-bleaching under open-circuit conditions. The assembled T-BWO-based self-bleaching ECD delivers a moderate optical modulation (ΔR) of (37.8 ± 1.7)% and excellent cycling stability (86% performance retention after 900 cycles). This work not only introduces a novel high-performance inorganic electrochromic material but also provides a new design paradigm for functional ECDs toward practical automotive antiglare applications.

title: Thermo-responsive Ionizable Xanthone Bolaamphiphiles for Dynamic Self-Assembly into Nanovesicles Enabling Enhanced Intracellular Drug Release and Tumor Growth Inhibition
abstract: Abstract Stimuli-responsive supramolecular nanocarriers capable of controlled drug release have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional chemotherapy; however, the development of structurally defined small-molecule systems exhibiting thermo-responsive behavior within biologically relevant temperature ranges remains challenging. Herein, we report a series of ionizable xanthone-based bolaamphiphiles (X1–X3) engineered to undergo temperature-triggered self-assembly in aqueous media. Systematic modulation of oxyethylene-chain density revealed that X3 exhibits a sharp and reversible lower critical solution temperature (LCST) transition within the physiological temperature window (35–40 °C), leading to the formation of stable nanovesicular assemblies. The resulting X3 nanovesicles accommodate doxorubicin (DOX) with an encapsulation efficiency of ∼25% and a drug-loading content of 11% while maintaining good colloidal stability under physiologically relevant conditions. X3-DOX nanovesicles exhibit progressive thermoresponsive drug release near physiological temperature, which is further enhanced under mild hyperthermia, together with an additional acid-responsive release behavior associated with protonation of the piperazine units (apparent pKa ≈ 4.5). Cellular studies performed in 4T1 breast cancer and A549 lung cancer cells demonstrated enhanced intracellular drug accumulation, superior cytotoxicity, and effective suppression of multicellular tumor spheroids compared with free DOX. Furthermore, the nanoformulation exhibited excellent hemocompatibility, favorable biodistribution characteristics, and efficient systemic clearance. In a 4T1 tumor-bearing mouse model, X3-DOX induced remarkable tumor-growth inhibition with minimal systemic toxicity. These findings establish thermo-responsive xanthone-based nanovesicles as a versatile supramolecular platform for controlled anticancer drug delivery and provide a molecularly defined strategy for developing stimuli-responsive nanomedicines.

title: Metal–Organic Framework@Polysulfone Composite Beads for Air Filtration of Postharvest Pathogenic Fungal Spores
abstract: Abstract Phytopathogenic fungal infections pose a persistent threat to postharvest fruit quality and food security worldwide, with resistant strains increasingly limiting the efficacy of conventional fungicides. This study explored metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) as an emerging class of antifungal materials and examined their potential for air-based decontamination in storage environments. Among the zinc- and copper-based frameworks tested, HKUST-1 and ZIF-8 demonstrated exceptionally broad-spectrum antifungal activity, completely inhibiting mycelial growth of Penicillium expansum, Penicillium citrinum, and Colletotrichum gloeosporioides, while maintaining strong inhibition of Botrytis cinerea and Mucor piriformis. To enable practical deployment, the most active MOFs were incorporated into polysulfone composite beads via phase inversion, preserving their antifungal properties while offering a processable and scalable format. In vitro assays revealed that these MOF@PSF beads substantially suppressed both mycelial growth and spore germination, with HKUST-1@PSF and ZIF-8@PSF composites reducing conidial viability to near-complete levels. Mechanistic studies revealed that HKUST-1 primarily acts through substantial copper ion release (≈19 ppm), leading to pronounced metabolic inhibition, whereas ZIF-8 operates via reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Evaluation in a dual-chamber air-filtration prototype demonstrated remarkable performance: both composites reduced airborne spore transfer by 95.2–96.7% for P. expansum and by 99.4–99.6% for B. cinerea, effectively preventing contamination of the clean chamber and protecting the stored produce. These findings establish MOF@PSF composite beads as bioactive filtration materials that combine physical spore capture with intrinsic antifungal action, offering a residue-free route to limiting fungal dissemination during postharvest storage.

title: Robust Thermal Stability, Flame Retardancy, and Weather Resistance Cross-Linked Cellulose Aerogel toward High-Performance Passive Radiative Cooling
abstract: Abstract The frequent occurrence of high temperatures has driven the development of green passive cooling technologies. Traditional passive radiative cooling materials have single performance, insufficient weather resistance and structural stability, and are unable to adapt to outdoor multifunctional thermal management. In this study, cellulose nanofibers were used as the substrate, and silica and methyltrimethoxysilane were incorporated to prepare a composite aerogel. Tests show that the optimal sample has excellent radiation cooling, heat insulation, flame retardancy, hydrophobicity, and sound absorption performance. With a solar reflectance of 93.5% and a mid-infrared emissivity of 94.3%, it provides a maximum outdoor temperature reduction of 15.7 °C. Its minimum thermal conductivity reaches 0.034 W m–1 K–1, offering excellent thermal insulation performance. The total heat release and the rate of heat release were significantly reduced, and flame retardancy was greatly improved. In addition, the sample exhibits a water contact angle of 137.2°, endowing it with favorable self-cleaning properties. The average sound absorption coefficient reaches 0.78 in the broadband range of 1000–6300 Hz, and the noise reduction performance is superior to that of commercial materials. This multifunctional composite aerogel overcomes the performance limitations of traditional materials and offers new insights into the development and application of outdoor integrated thermal management functional materials.

title: Correction to “ZnBr2-Assisted Br-Rich Regulation of Blue-Emitting CsPbBr3 Nanoplatelets Synthesized at Low Temperature”
3D Printed Sandpile-Shaped Photothermal Evaporator Based on Thiol-Ene Click Chemistry for Efficient Water Evaporation
abstract: Abstract The interface evaporation technology driven by solar energy has received widespread attention due to its advantages of being clean, pollution-free, and low in energy consumption. However, the cumbersome preparation process of existing high-efficiency evaporators hinders their large-scale promotion and application. Furthermore, we find that the inclined slope of the sandpile has the geometric condition of “forced reflection,” and the incident light can form reciprocating reflection between adjacent sandpiles, greatly improving the light capture efficiency and providing a structural basis for achieving efficient evaporation. Inspired by this, we construct a sandpile-shaped photothermal evaporator with different array densities by digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing technology with thiol-ene click chemistry reactions, using pentaerythritol tetrakis(3-mercaptopropionate) (PETMP) and poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) and molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) as photothermal materials to achieve integrated molding of the evaporator. Through structural optimization, the 3 × 3 array structure exhibits the best evaporation performance, with an evaporation rate of 1.91 kg m–2 h–1 and an evaporation efficiency of 90.9% at one solar intensity. When used for photocatalytic degradation of dye wastewater, the degradation efficiency of dyes can reach 86%. In addition, using a 3 × 3 array evaporator to treat salt-containing dye wastewater can cause directional salt collection due to the temperature difference between the top and bottom. After 5 complete evaporation and collection cycles, the average salt collection capacity of the evaporator can still be maintained at 0.593 g, with a salt collection rate of 158.34 mg m–2 h–1. This biomimetic photothermal evaporator provides a solution for the recycle and high purification of salt-containing dye wastewater.

title: Constructing Continuous Proton Channels through One-Dimensional Confined Nanofillers for High-Performance H2/O2 Fuel Cells
abstract: Abstract Establishing continuous proton transport pathways alongside robust interfacial interactions remains a critical bottleneck for organic–inorganic composite proton exchange membranes (PEMs). Herein, we report a rationally designed hybrid nanofiller (SUC@PHNTs) that integrates the long-range orientational order of one-dimensional (1D) halloysite nanotubes (HNTs) with the high-density proton-hopping sites of the metal-organic framework UiO-66-(COOH)2 (UC) and zwitterionic surface grafts. Subsequently when dispersed in a sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) (SPEEK) matrix, this 1D confined architecture bridges discrete UC domains into interconnected, continuous proton-conducting channels, effectively reducing proton transport tortuosity. Specifically, the S/SUC@PHNTs-3.0% membrane delivered 174.72 mS cm–1 (80 °C, 100% RH), corresponding to a 35.21% increase relative to pristine SPEEK. In an H2/O2 single-cell test, the membrane delivered a maximum power density of 793.29 mW cm–2, substantially exceeding that of SPEEK. Moreover, the voltage decay rate over 150 h of continuous operation was merely 0.42 mV h–1, indicative of excellent long-term operational stability. Overall, these results establish that the 1D confined nanofiller design strategy provides a promising technological pathway toward high-performance PEMs.

title: Regulating the Activity and Product Selectivity of Electrocatalytic Glycerol Oxidation by Changing the Au Loading on Ni2.86Te2/NF
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic glycerol oxidation reaction (GOR) has attracted much attention recently in the production of high-value-added chemicals coupled with water electrolysis for energy-saving hydrogen production due to its mild reaction conditions, green and harmless, and lower onset potential than the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in water electrolysis. However, under alkaline conditions, glycerol is prone to generate low-value-added C1 products, and the selectivity for C3 products is a significant challenge. In this work, we successfully regulated the activity and product selectivity of electrocatalytic glycerol oxidation by changing the Au loading on Ni2.86Te2/NF. The results showed that the selectivity of Au/Ni2.86Te2/NF-3 for glyceric acid (GLA) was 72.41%, and its GOR performance and selectivity were superior to those of recently reported catalysts. An appropriate Au loading results in favorable changes in Au distribution and surface electronic structure, which are associated with improved GOR activity and GLA selectivity.

title: Dicationic Porous Poly(Ionic Liquid)s with Hydrogen Bond Donors for Efficient Catalytic Conversion of CO2 under Mild Conditions
abstract: Abstract The formation of cyclic carbonates by coupling CO2 with epoxides offers a practical way of upgrading the surplus CO2 that has accumulated in the atmosphere, and thus helps to mitigate global warming. Because CO2 is intrinsically robust thermodynamically and sluggish kinetically, however, this transformation usually demands harsh conditions. Herein, a family of porous poly(ionic liquid)s denoted bAm-PIL-x (bAm = bis-amide) was constructed by radical copolymerization of an imidazolium-based ionic liquid monomer (tVIm-IL) and a quaternary ammonium-based ionic liquid monomer (tQAm-IL) in the presence of N,N'-methylenebisacrylamide as the cross-linker. These polymers combine a moderate specific surface area, pores spanning several size regimes, and a pronounced affinity for CO2, which makes them well suited to both capturing and converting CO2. Applied to the coupling of CO2 with epoxides under solvent-free, metal-free, and cocatalyst-free conditions, bAm-PIL-2 delivered excellent performance at a mild 80 °C and 1.0 bar. The catalyst was readily regenerated and recycled, and it accepted a wide range of epoxide substrates. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations together with in situ infrared spectroscopy were used to probe how the catalyst, the epoxides, and CO2 interact, and on this basis a plausible reaction mechanism for the cycloaddition is proposed. The present findings offer meaningful guidance for designing highly efficient catalysts for CO2 conversion.

title: Promoting Glycine Electrosynthesis from Nitrate and Oxalic Acid over Co–Cu Dual-Site Metal–Organic Frameworks
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical coreduction of nitrate (NO3–) and oxalic acid to glycine (ENOG) provides a sustainable alternative to conventional glycine production but remains limited by sluggish reactant activation, inefficient C–N coupling, and competing reaction pathways. Herein, a dual-site metal–organic framework, CoTAPc-BPDA-Cu, is developed as an efficient and robust cathode catalyst for ENOG. Operando spectroscopic measurements and theoretical calculations reveal the cooperative effect of Cu–Co dual sites in promoting OA-to-*C2H2O3 conversion, *NO3 reduction to *NH2OH, *C2H2O3-*NH2OH coupling to *C2H3NO3, and subsequent *C2H3NO3 hydrogenation for selective glycine formation. Moreover, by integrating cathodic ENOG over the CoTAPc-BPDA-Cu catalyst with an anodic glycerol oxidation over the PbO2 catalyst in a two-electrode electrolyzer, we achieve a glycine Faradaic efficiency of 78.3% and a glycine yield rate of 629.3 mmol h−1 g−1, while enabling the gram-scale production of high-purity glycine.

title: Biomimetic Liquid Diodes Across Materials and Scales for Directional Liquid Transfer
abstract: Abstract The last decade has witnessed remarkable advancements in liquid diode, evolving from fundamental research to cutting-edge applications such as microfluidics, thermal management, and wearable electronics. However, how material characteristics and structural scales mediate liquid transport on liquid diodes has yet to be fully clarified to date. In this study, we develop a Crassula muscosa inspired liquid diode (CMLD) with superior material adaptability and structural scale adaptability spanning three orders of magnitude. Such a liquid diode endows a cross-material, and cross-scale unidirectional liquid transfer from microscale to macroscale. The mechanisms underlying the role of the wettability, viscosity and structure scale in regulating the liquid transfer kinetics including transfer distance, transfer velocity and liquid rectification, are clearly demonstrated. By combining experimental observation, numerical simulation, and building a theoretical retention force model, the liquid transfer and pinning mechanisms governed by asymmetric reentrant structures are systematically elucidated, which enables superior robustness for unidirectional liquid transfer of continuous flows with various flow rates. These results provide a robust framework for coupling material characteristics and structural scales to achieve controllable unidirectional liquid transfer, laying a solid foundation for the practical implementation of liquid diode-based technologies.

title: Resolving the Structural Origin of Lattice Oxygen Release across Scales in Practical Lithium‐Manganese‐Rich Electrodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Gas evolution from lattice oxygen release is a major obstacle to deployment of high‐energy‐density cathodes, yet its structural origin within dense electrodes remains challenging to resolve across multiple length scales. This difficulty arises because gas evolution is the collective outcome of oxygen release from numerous grains and particles, whose environments can vary across electrode, secondary‐particle, and grain scales. Here, by integrating online electrochemical mass spectrometry with synchrotron X‐ray and electron microscopy, this study resolves the spatial origin of O 2 evolution through mapping Mn reduction, a chemical fingerprint of oxygen release, across four orders of magnitude in length scale. Two lithium‐manganese‐rich layered oxide (LMR) electrodes that vary only in secondary‐particle size are employed as a model system, and their O 2 evolution differs twofold. Spatially resolving Mn oxidation state distribution reveals no detectable Mn‐reduction gradient across the electrode thickness or within particles, indicating that the difference does not originate from electrode‐ or particle‐scale heterogeneity. Instead, frontal facets (lithium‐intercalation planes) of grains exhibit deeper Mn reduction and surface reconstruction than lateral facets, consistent with favorable oxygen vacancy formation and migration. O 2 evolution matches after frontal‐facet area normalization, identifying frontal‐facet exposure as a key structural descriptor for O 2 evolution in these practical LMR electrodes.

title: Regioisomerism‐Guided Molecular Passivation for 26.05%‐Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Defect‐mediated nonradiative recombination remains a major barrier to efficient and stable perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Although considerable advances have been made with molecular additives, how the spatial arrangement of functional groups affects device performance remains largely unexplored. Here, we present a regioisomerism‐guided molecular design strategy using fluorinated aniline as a well‐defined model system to incorporate into the lead iodide (PbI 2 ) precursor solution during two‐step sequential perovskite deposition. By systematically comparing ortho‐, meta‐, and para‐fluoroaniline, we demonstrate that the ortho isomer, 2‐fluoroaniline (2‐FA), affords the most effective regulation of defect states and device performance. This superiority arises from the formation of an intramolecular hydrogen bond, which redistributes the molecular electrostatic potential and confers stable bidentate coordination with the perovskite lattice. Additionally, 2‐FA facilitates high‐quality α‐FAPbI 3 films and aligns the energy level favorably with the hole transport layer, yielding a champion efficiency of 26.05% for the n‐i‐p PSCs. Moreover, the 2‐FA‐containing device exhibits superior operational stability. This regioisomerism‐guided design works universally across n‐i‐p and p‐i‐n architectures, irrespective of one‐step or two‐step fabrication. Our work establishes regioisomerism as a simple yet powerful molecular design principle for molecular engineering and provides new insight into the rational development of efficient and stable PSCs.

title: Intermolecular Interaction Engineering for Efficient Large‐Area Tin‐based Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Poly(3,4‐ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) has been widely used as a hole transport layer (HTL) in environmentally friendly tin‐based perovskite solar cells (TPSCs). However, its intrinsic weak acidity and strong tendency toward molecular aggregates hinder its performance in TPSCs. Here, we develop a molecular engineering strategy by introducing a p‐type small molecule, 4,4'‐(5,6‐bis(2‐methoxyethoxy)benzo[c][1,2,5]thiadiazole‐4,7‐diyl)bis(2,5‐difluoro‐N,N‐bis(4‐methoxyphenyl)aniline) (FEG), to modify PEDOT:PSS and, crucially, employ a comprehensive set of solid‐state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) techniques to directly elucidate the intermolecular interactions governing this modification. Magic‐angle spinning 1 H NMR, 1 H‐ 1 H double‐quantum‐single‐quantum correlation spectroscopy, and variable spinning‐rate measurements reveal strong interactions between FEG and PSS that redistribute the PEDOT:PSS microstructure and promote greater charge delocalization within the conductive polymer network. This interaction improves PEDOT:PSS dispersion, neutralizes residual acidity and enhances interfacial wettability, enabling the growth of high‐quality Sn‐based perovskite films with enlarged grains, reduced defect density and relieved residual stress. As a result, trap‐assisted recombination is suppressed and hole extraction is improved. Consequently, FEG‐PEDOT:PSS‐based TPSCs achieve a record efficiency of 14.92% for 1‐cm 2 devices and a champion efficiency of 17.02% for 0.04‐cm 2 devices, substantially outperforming their pristine PEDOT counterparts. Furthermore, these devices exhibit excellent operational stability, maintaining over 85% of their initial efficiency after 1100 h of storage under a N 2 atmosphere.

title: Programmable Engineered Living Vehicles as Autonomous Biofactories for Synergistic Osteomyelitis Management and Bone Regeneration
abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional static biomaterials and synthetic nanomedicines struggle to penetrate recalcitrant biofilms and orchestrate tissue regeneration in deep‐seated infections due to limited autonomous navigation and a lack of spatiotemporal responsiveness. Here, we conceptualize and develop a programmable engineered living vehicle (ELV) that functions as an autonomous biofactory for the synergistic management of drug‐resistant osteomyelitis. Built upon a self‐propelled Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 chassis with innate ecological dominance, these living biofactories are hierarchically equipped with environmental biosensors and logic‐gated computing modules. Crucially, leveraging AlphaFold 3‐guided molecular docking, we engineered multiscale thermo‐responsive genetic logic circuits that enable precise, temperature‐dependent biomanufacturing of bacteriolytic lysostaphin (LYS) and vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) (≥37°C), coupled with a fail‐safe thermal self‐destruct mechanism (≥42°C). Furthermore, surface‐engineered (DSS) 6 peptides confer robust hydroxyapatite affinity, acting as a bone‐homing navigation module. In a rat osteomyelitis model induced by methicillin‐resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), intravenously deployed ELV biofactories autonomously navigate to the infected niche, actively penetrate biofilms, and outperform vancomycin in pathogen clearance. Concurrently, localized payload secretion reprograms the osteo‐immune microenvironment, significantly accelerating bone repair. This work establishes a versatile paradigm for next‐generation smart living therapeutics, bridging synthetic biology with micro‐engineering to address complex clinical challenges.

title: Activation‐Free and Strain‐Resilient Island‐Bridge Liquid Metal Inks for Machine‐Learning‐Enabled Epidermal Electromyography
abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid metal particle‐based inks offer a scalable route toward stretchable electronics, yet their practical implementation is hindered by activation‐dependent conductivity and poor electrical stability under deformation. Herein, we report an intrinsically conductive and strain‐resilient liquid metal ink with a rationally engineered island‐bridge micro‐architecture, in which Cu‐decorated carbon nanotubes (CuCNTs) bridge adjacent liquid metal particles (LMPs) through initial hydrogen‐bonding/coordination‐assisted attachment to the native gallium‐oxide shell, followed by local Cu‐Ga alloying at the CuCNTs/LMPs interface. Enabled by solvent‐mediated dispersion and interfacial hybridization, the strain‐resilient composite ink supports high‐resolution (100 µm) screen printing and deformable circuit integration. The dynamically reconfigurable island‐bridge network retains a sheet resistance of 1.3 × 10 −1 Ω sq −1 at 300% strain, together with stable resistance during prolonged cyclic stretching and bending. When printed into a compact 12‐channel array on breathable fibrous substrates, the resulting electrode array exhibits low skin‐electrode impedance and superior high‐density surface electromyography (HD‐sEMG) performance compared with commercial gel electrodes. Combined with machine‐learning‐assisted analysis, the electromyography arrays enable training‐state recognition, individualized load assessment, and continuous monitoring of fatigue‐associated exercise states during dynamic exercise. This work provides a scalable strategy for intrinsically conductive liquid metal electronics and advances their application in intelligent wearable biointerfaces and soft electronic systems.

title: Time‐Encoded Ligand Presentation via a Magnetically Actuated Hydrogel Mitigates T Cell Exhaustion
abstract: ABSTRACT Adoptive T cell therapy (ACT) requires ex vivo expansion of tumor‐reactive CD8 + T cells, yet prolonged antigenic stimulation frequently induces exhaustion, limiting persistence and therapeutic efficacy. Here, we present a magnetically actuated, extracellular matrix–mimetic hydrogel that enables reversible control of T cell receptor (TCR) stimulation timing. By embedding αCD3ε/αCD28‐functionalized magnetic nanoparticles within a soft hyaluronic acid matrix, external magnetic fields dynamically expose or conceal stimulatory ligands, allowing programmable alternation between activation and rest. Continuous ligand presentation sustains TCR signaling and drives inhibitory receptor expression and functional exhaustion. In contrast, alternating activation–rest cycles periodically attenuate proximal TCR signaling, reduce exhaustion‐associated marker expression, and bias differentiation toward central memory‐like states while preserving cytokine production and recall capacity. T cells expanded under intermittent stimulation exhibit enhanced antigen‐specific cytotoxicity, reduced dependence on PD‐1 blockade, and superior tumor control in vivo, together with increased CD8 + T cell abundance across analyzed tissues. These results identify temporal control of mechanochemical signaling as a materials‐encoded regulator of T cell fate and provide a non‐genetic strategy for generating functionally competent T cell products with reduced exhaustion‐associated dysfunction and improved antitumor activity.

title: Adaptive Supramolecular Interactions Govern Redox‐Active Molecules in Aqueous Redox Flow Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Weak noncovalent interactions critically govern molecular behavior in solution, yet how they shape redox processes in aqueous electrochemical environments remains underexplored. Here, we demonstrate control over the solubility and redox stability of aromatic redox‐active molecules in aqueous redox flow batteries (RFBs). Zwitterionic substitution of naphthalene diimide (NDI) bearing quaternary ammonium and sulfonate groups shows weak π–π cohesion through steric and electrostatic effects, rendering otherwise insoluble NDIs responsive to external anions. Hydrophobic and weakly hydrated anions such as iodide and bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide disrupt residual stacking through anion–π interactions, enabling dissolution to concentrations approaching 1.3 M. Upon electrochemical reduction, these anions dissociate, and the reduced NDI species are instead stabilized through spin pairing and cation‐mediated intermolecular interactions, which suppress irreversible aggregation, slow self‐discharge, and enable rapid redox reactions. Operando Raman spectroscopy, 1 H NMR, and EPR elucidate the redox‐state‐dependent evolution of these supramolecular assemblies. Together, these results establish zwitterionic molecular design for adaptive supramolecular redox chemistry in aqueous RFBs.

title: Lewis‐Basic Metal Sulfide Electrode Interfaces Unlock High Power Density Alkaline All‐Iron Redox Flow Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Alkaline all‐iron redox flow batteries (AIRFBs) are promising for safe, low‐cost grid‐scale energy storage using Earth‐abundant elements. However, insufficient energy efficiency and power density limit practical deployment, while the interfacial kinetic origin of these losses remains unclear. Here, we identify sluggish outer‐sphere electron‐transfer kinetics of Fe‐chelate anolytes as a key kinetic bottleneck governing polarization in alkaline AIRFBs and further link this bottleneck to limited outer Helmholtz plane (OHP)‐region accessibility and weak interfacial electronic coupling. To overcome this limitation, we develop Lewis‐basic sulfide interfaces that regulate the local Fe‐chelate/electrode environment. These regulated interfaces convert inefficient diffusion encounters into productive sulfide‐assisted outer‐sphere electron‐transfer events, thereby accelerating anolyte redox kinetics and suppressing polarization. An alkaline AIRFB assembled with a Ni 3 S 4 ‐modified electrode delivers an energy efficiency of 80.65% at 200 mA cm −2 and a peak power density of 501.2 mW cm −2 , compared with 65.69% and 185.5 mW cm −2 for the pristine cell. The Ni 3 S 4 ‐based cell further maintains an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.9%, an average energy efficiency of 77.8%, and stable operation over 3000 cycles at 200 mA cm −2 . This work reveals an interfacial kinetic bottleneck in alkaline AIRFBs and establishes Lewis‐basic interface engineering as a strategy for high‐power and low‐cost long‐duration energy storage.

title: Stabilizing Ru Sites via Lattice Oxygen Locking of Nb‐Ru/RuO 2 to Break the Activity–Stability Trade‐Off for Acidic Oxygen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing highly active and stable Ru‐based catalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is essential to accelerate the industrialization of proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE). However, Ru‐based catalysts inevitably follow the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) during the actual reaction, which in turn triggers severe Ru dissolution. While shifting the reaction pathway to the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) improves stability, it often compromises catalytic activity. Herein, we design an Nb‐doped Ru/RuO 2 heterostructure catalyst to inhibit the unstable LOM, and concurrently propose a favorable Brønsted Site‐Promoted Proton Transfer (BSPT) mechanism derived from the AEM. Specifically, the synergy between Nb doping and Ru/RuO 2 heterostructure enhances activity by improving deprotonation capability and optimizing oxygen‐intermediate adsorption, while simultaneously improving durability by stabilizing lattice oxygen and suppressing excessive oxidation and dissolution of Ru. Consequently, the Nb‐Ru/RuO 2 delivers an overpotential of 186 mV at 10 mA cm −2 with impressive durability over 3000 h. In a working PEMWE, it exhibits remarkable durability for 3000, 1200, and 900 h at 500, 1000, and 2000 mA cm −2 . This study offers novel design principles and theoretical foundations to advance efficient, low‐cost PEMWE hydrogen production.

title: Emergent Molecular Weaving in an Ionic Metal‐Organic Network for CO 2 Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular weaving has emerged as a powerful design strategy in supramolecular chemistry, yet most woven frameworks rely on rigid ligands and elaborate templating. Here, we report a minimalistic, aqueous‐phase synthesis of a woven metal‐organic superstructure assembled from Cu 2+ and 2,4,6‐trinitrobenzene‐1,3,5‐triol (TNPG). In the crystal, asymmetric coordination of TNPG with Cu 2+ yields charged one‐dimensional (1D) polymeric strands featuring both distorted octahedral and square planar geometries. These strands interlace at a specific angle to form a two‐dimensional (2D) woven architecture, a rare 1D─1D topological weaving stabilized by hydrogen bonding. The structure also incorporates discrete Cu 2+ cationic complexes, where metal coordination significantly perturbs the aromatic π‐conjugated system of TNPG. These cationic units are tethered within the network through strong hydrogen bonding and electrostatic attraction to the anionic woven strands, contributing to the structural integrity of the superstructure. Given the redox‐active Cu 2+ centers, electronically modulated ligand environment, and framework stability, the Cu‐TNPG network was evaluated for visible‐light‐driven CO 2 reduction. The photocatalytic performance of Cu‐TNPG originates from its high charge separation efficiency and abundant catalytically active sites. Moreover, mild thermal pre‐activation led to enhanced CO evolution efficiency through structural modulations, with a selectivity of ∼85% for CO over H 2 , highlighting its structural and functional versatility.

title: Natural Versus Artificial Photosynthesis: Pushing Beyond Nature's Limits to Deliver Low‐Cost Solar Fuels
abstract: ABSTRACT Natural photosynthesis (NP) sustains life by coordinating light harvesting, charge separation, multielectron catalysis, carbon fixation, regulation, and repair. Artificial photosynthesis instead aims to convert solar energy selectively into fuels and chemicals through designed light absorbers, interfaces, and catalytic sites. This review compares the two systems across light harvesting, charge separation and transfer, catalytic conversion, photoprotection, and system integration, emphasizing that meaningful comparisons require similar functions, comparable metrics, and clearly defined system boundaries. Field‐scale NP typically operates at sub‐percent solar‐to‐biomass efficiencies, whereas selected artificial photosynthetic devices have achieved double‐digit solar‐to‐fuel efficiencies under defined conditions. These values should not be directly ranked because the products and system functions differ. We identify the respective strengths of artificial systems in spectral, interfacial, catalytic, and product control, and of natural systems in regulation, repair, regeneration, and multiscale coordination, providing design principles for efficient, durable, and scalable solar‐to‐chemical conversion.

title: A Precursor Design Principle for Archipelagic Hard‐Carbon Structural Evolution Through Cohesion–Solvation Regulation of Asphaltene Molecular Heterogeneity
abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium‐ion batteries are central to the development of affordable electrochemical storage for renewable energy integration. Yet hard‐carbon anode design lacks a precursor‐level principle linking molecular assembly in chemically heterogeneous feedstocks to oxidative stabilization and closed‐pore formation. Here we establish a precursor‐level cohesion‐solvation design principle for regulating molecular selection and assembly in heterogeneous aromatic feedstocks. Toluene‐fractionated asphaltene precursors undergo oxidative crosslinking, redirecting carbonization from continuous coke‐like growth toward separated turbostratic domains and confined closed pores. A hard‐carbon performance screening index (HPSI) quantifies structural and electrochemical performance, while density functional theory (DFT) reveals stronger Na affinity and lower migration barriers in defect‐engineered carbon galleries. The solvent‐selected AHC‐80‐1400 delivers 400.1 mAh g −1 at 0.05 A g −1 with 87.7% ICE and retains 92.3% capacity after 10 000 cycles, while sustaining wide‐temperature sodium storage with 91.8% and 90.4% retention at −20°C and 50°C, respectively. At scale, a 10‐kg batch enables a 1.18 Ah NFM||AHC‐80‐1400 pouch cell, delivering 163.3 Wh kg −1 and 95.5% retention after 700 cycles. A cradle‐to‐gate life‐cycle assessment (LCA) shows that AHC‐80‐1400 production reduces climate‐change impact by 33.7% relative to Commercial HC. These findings establish precursor‐stage molecular selection as a design principle for harnessing feedstock heterogeneity to control carbonization trajectories and electrochemical function.

title: 3D Ordered Macroporous Cu‐Based Multimetallic Alloy Enables Efficient Asymmetric C–C Coupling for Selective CO 2 Electroreduction to Ethylene
abstract: ABSTRACT The abundant Cu 0 /Cu δ+ interfaces generated after reconstruction are crucial for promoting the coupling of *CO and *COH intermediates in electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction. However, Cu sites derived from a single metal severely restrict C–C coupling efficiency and product selectivity. Here, the direct regulation of the interfacial microenvironment is reported by constructing a 3D ordered macroporous (3DOM) architecture composed of multimetallic alloy (MMA) on the surface of CuO x . The designed catalyst exhibits superior Faradic efficiency of 64.1% for electrochemical CO 2 reduction to ethylene at −1.55 V versus RHE under acidic conditions, and stability for over 60 h at 600 mA cm −2 in a flow cell. In‐situ experiments and theoretical simulations reveal that the 3DOM structure enhances the surface electric field, raises the local pH, and accelerates interfacial mass transport. The electronic structure of Cu δ+ (0δ+ sites could govern *CO adsorption and hydrogenation pathways, thereby enhancing ethylene selectivity.
